components.title: Rego Policy Libraries
components.description: Open Policy Agent (Rego) compliance and security policy library, version 2.4.2: evaluates the controls in the referenced catalogs from machine-collected facts and emits a compliance_report per framework.
components.purpose: Automated evaluation of the referenced controls; produces OSCAL assessment-results, SARIF and OCSF findings.

implemented-requirements.description: Evaluated by Rego package aca_155_260.main (frameworks/privacy/aca_155_260/aca_155_260_main.rego): Where the Exchange creates or collects personally identifiable information for the purposes of determining eligibility for enrollment in a qualified health plan; determining eligibility for other insurance affordability programs, as defined in § 155.300; or determining eligibility for exemptions from the individual shared responsibility provisions in section 5000A of the Code, the Exchange may only use or disclose such personally identifiable information to the extent such information is necessary: (i) For the Exchange to carry out the functions described in § 155.200; (ii) For the Exchange to carry out other functions not described in paragraph (a)(1)(i) of this section, which the Secretary determines to be in compliance with section 1411(g)(2)(A) of the Affordable Care Act and for which an individual provides consent for his or her information to be used or disclosed; or (iii) For the Exchange to carry out other functions not described in paragraphs (a)(1)(i) and (ii) of this section, for which an individual provides consent for his or her information to be used or disclosed, and which the Secretary determines are in compliance with section 1411(g)(2)(A) of the Affordable Care Act under the following substantive and procedural requirements:

Evaluated by Rego package aca_155_260.main (frameworks/privacy/aca_155_260/aca_155_260_main.rego): To seek approval for a use or disclosure of personally identifiable information created or collected as described in paragraph (a)(1) of this section that is not described in paragraphs (a)(1)(i) or (ii) of this section, the Exchange must submit the following information to HHS: (1) Identity of the Exchange and appropriate contact persons; (2) Detailed description of the proposed use or disclosure, which must include, but not necessarily be limited to, a listing or description of the specific information to be used or disclosed and an identification of the persons or entities that may access or receive the information; (3) Description of how the use or disclosure will ensure the efficient operation of the Exchange consistent with section 1411(g)(2)(A) of the Affordable Care Act; and (4) Description of how the information to be used or disclosed will be protected in compliance with privacy and security standards that meet the requirements of this section or other relevant law, as applicable.

Evaluated by Rego package aca_155_260.main (frameworks/privacy/aca_155_260/aca_155_260_main.rego): The Exchange may not create, collect, use, or disclose personally identifiable information unless the creation, collection, use, or disclosure is consistent with this section.

Evaluated by Rego package apra_cps234.main (frameworks/financial/apra_cps234/cps234_main.rego): Robust mechanisms detect and respond to information security incidents in a timely manner
Evaluated by Rego package apra_cps234.main (frameworks/financial/apra_cps234/cps234_main.rego): Information security response plans are maintained for incidents that could plausibly occur

Evaluated by Rego package apra_cps234.main (frameworks/financial/apra_cps234/cps234_main.rego): Response plans include mechanisms for managing all stages from detection to post-incident review, and for escalation and reporting to the Board, governing bodies and responsible individuals

Evaluated by Rego package apra_cps234.main (frameworks/financial/apra_cps234/cps234_main.rego): Information security response plans are reviewed and tested annually to ensure they remain effective and fit-for-purpose

Evaluated by Rego package apra_cps234.main (frameworks/financial/apra_cps234/cps234_main.rego): Control effectiveness is tested through a systematic testing program whose nature and frequency match the rate of change in threats, asset criticality and sensitivity, incident consequences, exposure to untrusted environments, and the materiality and frequency of change

Evaluated by Rego package apra_cps234.main (frameworks/financial/apra_cps234/cps234_main.rego): Where reliance is placed on a related party's or third party's control testing, the nature and frequency of that testing is assessed against paragraph 27(a)–(e)

Evaluated by Rego package apra_cps234.main (frameworks/financial/apra_cps234/cps234_main.rego): Testing results that identify control deficiencies which cannot be remediated in a timely manner are escalated and reported to the Board or senior management
Evaluated by Rego package apra_cps234.main (frameworks/financial/apra_cps234/cps234_main.rego): Testing is conducted by appropriately skilled and functionally independent specialists

Evaluated by Rego package apra_cps234.main (frameworks/financial/apra_cps234/cps234_main.rego): The sufficiency of the testing program is reviewed at least annually or on material change to information assets or the business environment

Evaluated by Rego package apra_cps234.main (frameworks/financial/apra_cps234/cps234_main.rego): Internal audit reviews the design and operating effectiveness of information security controls, including those maintained by related and third parties (control assurance)
Evaluated by Rego package apra_cps234.main (frameworks/financial/apra_cps234/cps234_main.rego): Information security control assurance is provided by appropriately skilled personnel

Evaluated by Rego package apra_cps234.main (frameworks/financial/apra_cps234/cps234_main.rego): Internal audit assesses control assurance provided by a related or third party where an incident could materially affect the entity or its customers and audit intends to rely on that assurance

Evaluated by Rego package apra_cps234.main (frameworks/financial/apra_cps234/cps234_main.rego): APRA is notified as soon as possible and no later than 72 hours after becoming aware of an information security incident that materially affected (or could materially affect) the entity or its customers, or that was notified to another regulator

Evaluated by Rego package apra_cps234.main (frameworks/financial/apra_cps234/cps234_main.rego): APRA is notified as soon as possible and no later than 10 business days after becoming aware of a material control weakness the entity expects not to remediate in a timely manner

Evaluated by Rego package apra_cps234.main (frameworks/financial/apra_cps234/cps234_main.rego): apra_cps234.third_party_managed_assets must be declared true or false — whether related parties or third parties manage information assets cannot be assumed
Evaluated by Rego package apra_cps234.main (frameworks/financial/apra_cps234/cps234_main.rego): CPS 234 para %v (%v): %v — not attested
Evaluated by Rego package apra_cps234.main (frameworks/financial/apra_cps234/cps234_main.rego): attestation for unknown paragraph %v — requirements are paragraphs 13–36

control-implementations.description: Controls of bnm_rmit evaluated by the Rego Policy Libraries (107 controls, 1 Rego modules).

implemented-requirements.description: Evaluated by Rego package bnm_rmit.main (frameworks/financial/bnm_rmit/rmit_main.rego): RMiT 11.4 — whether the institution is designated a National Critical Information Infrastructure entity under the Cyber Security Act 2024 must be declared true or false

Evaluated by Rego package bnm_rmit.main (frameworks/financial/bnm_rmit/rmit_main.rego): RMiT 10.12, 10.46–10.49 — whether third-party service providers are engaged for technology functions must be declared true or false

Evaluated by Rego package bnm_rmit.main (frameworks/financial/bnm_rmit/rmit_main.rego): RMiT §12 — whether the institution provides digital services or delivery channels to customers must be declared true or false
Evaluated by Rego package bnm_rmit.main (frameworks/financial/bnm_rmit/rmit_main.rego): RMiT 10.50/10.52 — whether the institution uses cloud services must be declared true or false

Evaluated by Rego package bnm_rmit.main (frameworks/financial/bnm_rmit/rmit_main.rego): Technology project governance is commensurate with risk and complexity: oversight roles, authority and reporting structures, and risk assessments throughout the project life cycle

Evaluated by Rego package bnm_rmit.main (frameworks/financial/bnm_rmit/rmit_main.rego): Changes to source code of critical systems undergo source code review for security and recognised coding practices before introduction

Evaluated by Rego package bnm_rmit.main (frameworks/financial/bnm_rmit/rmit_main.rego): System changes are independently reviewed and approved; contingency plans for unsuccessful material changes are established and tested

Evaluated by Rego package bnm_rmit.main (frameworks/financial/bnm_rmit/rmit_main.rego): Contracts for critical systems developed or maintained by third parties require sufficient notice of impacting changes, demonstrated secure-by-design development, and continued accessibility of source code for business continuity

Evaluated by Rego package bnm_rmit.main (frameworks/financial/bnm_rmit/rmit_main.rego): Decommissioning of critical systems minimises customer and business impact, with contingency plans established and tested for unsuccessful decommissioning
Evaluated by Rego package bnm_rmit.main (frameworks/financial/bnm_rmit/rmit_main.rego): Robust policies identify and reduce shadow IT risks

Evaluated by Rego package bnm_rmit.main (frameworks/financial/bnm_rmit/rmit_main.rego): No system or digital service runs with known security vulnerabilities, on outdated platforms or end-of-life technology: a current security hardening baseline, timely patching, remedial plans for approaching EOL, and management-approved, risk-assessed, annually reviewed exceptions with phase-out timelines

Evaluated by Rego package bnm_rmit.main (frameworks/financial/bnm_rmit/rmit_main.rego): A patch and EOL management framework covers asset identification and risk assessment, deployment criteria, priority and turnaround by severity, compatibility testing, an end-to-end approval, testing, monitoring and tracking workflow, and end-user awareness

Evaluated by Rego package bnm_rmit.main (frameworks/financial/bnm_rmit/rmit_main.rego): The effectiveness and security of technology in use is monitored against disruptive developments (e.g. quantum computing): board advice on impact, a long-term strategy with competent resources, and a migration roadmap

Evaluated by Rego package bnm_rmit.main (frameworks/financial/bnm_rmit/rmit_main.rego): Project risk assessments address resource adequacy including vendors and concurrent projects, system complexity and integration, security controls through the life cycle, completeness of user requirements, robustness of testing, deployment and fallback strategies, and disaster recovery readiness

Evaluated by Rego package bnm_rmit.main (frameworks/financial/bnm_rmit/rmit_main.rego): A cryptography policy requires industry-standard algorithms, message authentication, hashes, signatures and random number generation; secure key life-cycle management; at least annual review of standards and algorithms for critical and customer-facing systems; an asset inventory of cryptographic tools and algorithms with rationale and mappings; and tested compromise-recovery plans

Evaluated by Rego package bnm_rmit.main (frameworks/financial/bnm_rmit/rmit_main.rego): Cryptographic controls are evaluated with due diligence; the institution retains ownership and control of encryption keys (or with an independent custodian) except for non-critical systems without customer information, manages externally generated keys to industry standards, weighs reliance on third-party assessments against risk appetite, and considers resource impact and reduced traffic visibility

Evaluated by Rego package bnm_rmit.main (frameworks/financial/bnm_rmit/rmit_main.rego): Cryptographic protocols for secret and public keys follow recognised international standards and are tested; secret and private key storage and computation occur in a protected environment (HSM, TEE or equivalent) commensurate with risk

Evaluated by Rego package bnm_rmit.main (frameworks/financial/bnm_rmit/rmit_main.rego): Public keys are stored in certificates from a Certificate Authority (recognised CAs for customers); authentication and signature protocols protect private keys so their use is legally binding; issuance and renewal follow industry and legal specifications
Evaluated by Rego package bnm_rmit.main (frameworks/financial/bnm_rmit/rmit_main.rego): Resilience and availability objectives of data centres are specified to support business recovery objectives
Evaluated by Rego package bnm_rmit.main (frameworks/financial/bnm_rmit/rmit_main.rego): Data centres have redundant capacity components and multiple distribution paths with no single point of failure

Evaluated by Rego package bnm_rmit.main (frameworks/financial/bnm_rmit/rmit_main.rego): Critical systems are hosted in dedicated, physically secured production data centre space not in a disaster-prone area, with no single point of failure in hardware, electrical, thermal and infrastructure design, and with adequate maintenance and continuous monitoring with timely alerts

Evaluated by Rego package bnm_rmit.main (frameworks/financial/bnm_rmit/rmit_main.rego): Data centre operations have control procedures including automated batch management, production change procedures, error handling and exception management

Evaluated by Rego package bnm_rmit.main (frameworks/financial/bnm_rmit/rmit_main.rego): Incompatible activities in data centre operations are segregated (development from operations); necessary vendor or programmer access to production is authorised and monitored
Evaluated by Rego package bnm_rmit.main (frameworks/financial/bnm_rmit/rmit_main.rego): System capacity is planned and managed for peak periods, growth plans and architecture changes

Evaluated by Rego package bnm_rmit.main (frameworks/financial/bnm_rmit/rmit_main.rego): The board and senior management receive and review timely reports on significant project risks throughout implementation

Evaluated by Rego package bnm_rmit.main (frameworks/financial/bnm_rmit/rmit_main.rego): Real-time monitoring tracks capacity utilisation and performance of key processes and services with actionable alerts; scope, metrics and thresholds are updated periodically

Evaluated by Rego package bnm_rmit.main (frameworks/financial/bnm_rmit/rmit_main.rego): Key digital services and delivery channels are made resilient: early-warning mechanisms by 30 September 2027 (detect failed transactions and measure availability, monitor affected customers and volumes, escalate immediately when 5% or more of expected daily customers or transactions are affected), regular reviews of vulnerable interdependencies, and stand-in processing arrangements by 30 September 2027 prioritised for the least substitutable channels with customers informed of terms, risks and responsibilities

Evaluated by Rego package bnm_rmit.main (frameworks/financial/bnm_rmit/rmit_main.rego): Critical systems with an expectation of immediate customer or counterparty service are designed for high availability: cumulative unplanned downtime at the customer interface of not more than 4 hours on a rolling 12 months and a maximum tolerable downtime of 120 minutes per incident

Evaluated by Rego package bnm_rmit.main (frameworks/financial/bnm_rmit/rmit_main.rego): Diversity in technology is prioritised so critical systems infrastructure is not excessively exposed to similar technology risks

Evaluated by Rego package bnm_rmit.main (frameworks/financial/bnm_rmit/rmit_main.rego): During digital service interruptions the institution escalates and decides promptly to resume via alternatives within the 10.32 timeframe, defines accountabilities and third-party arrangements for degradation, runs a communication plan with immediate customer notice, feedback handling, frequent updates and alternatives, offers a convenient availability-status check (e.g. real-time status on the website), and discloses its quarterly availability track record within 15 calendar days of quarter-end from 15 October 2027
Evaluated by Rego package bnm_rmit.main (frameworks/financial/bnm_rmit/rmit_main.rego): A reliable, scalable and secure enterprise network supports business activities and growth plans

Evaluated by Rego package bnm_rmit.main (frameworks/financial/bnm_rmit/rmit_main.rego): Network services for critical systems are reliable with no single point of failure against network faults and cyber threats

Evaluated by Rego package bnm_rmit.main (frameworks/financial/bnm_rmit/rmit_main.rego): Real-time bandwidth monitoring and network resilience metrics flag over-utilisation and disruptions from congestion and faults, including traffic analysis for trends and anomalies

Evaluated by Rego package bnm_rmit.main (frameworks/financial/bnm_rmit/rmit_main.rego): An enterprise technology architecture framework gives a comprehensive view of technology and baseline components, a technical design showing infrastructure, interconnectivity, dependencies and security controls (to find single points of failure), mappings to business functions, units, applications and data, principles for network and security design, and longer-term priorities
Evaluated by Rego package bnm_rmit.main (frameworks/financial/bnm_rmit/rmit_main.rego): Network services supporting critical systems ensure confidentiality, integrity and availability of data

Evaluated by Rego package bnm_rmit.main (frameworks/financial/bnm_rmit/rmit_main.rego): A maintained network design blueprint identifies all internal and external interfaces and connectivity, physical and logical, with segmentation
Evaluated by Rego package bnm_rmit.main (frameworks/financial/bnm_rmit/rmit_main.rego): Sufficient network device logs are retained for investigation and forensics for at least three years

Evaluated by Rego package bnm_rmit.main (frameworks/financial/bnm_rmit/rmit_main.rego): Safeguards (e.g. logical network segmentation from other group entities) minimise the risk of a compromise in one entity affecting others in the group

Evaluated by Rego package bnm_rmit.main (frameworks/financial/bnm_rmit/rmit_main.rego): A backup strategy and procedures manage the backup life cycle, keep adequate copies of critical data, OS, programs, utilities, master and transaction files and event logs, store media in an environmentally secure access-controlled site, secure removable media per Appendix 1, test restoration periodically with prompt root-cause remediation, and have an independent risk assessment of end-to-end backup storage and delivery

Evaluated by Rego package bnm_rmit.main (frameworks/financial/bnm_rmit/rmit_main.rego): A tamper-proof backup arrangement and an isolated recovery environment enable resumption of critical banking and payment services within tolerance after destructive cyber attacks such as ransomware

Evaluated by Rego package bnm_rmit.main (frameworks/financial/bnm_rmit/rmit_main.rego): The board and senior management exercise effective oversight of third-party service providers for critical technology functions; the institution remains accountable for all resulting risks

Evaluated by Rego package bnm_rmit.main (frameworks/financial/bnm_rmit/rmit_main.rego): Due diligence on third-party service providers is conducted before on-boarding and throughout the engagement, considering at least the Appendix 8 risks

Evaluated by Rego package bnm_rmit.main (frameworks/financial/bnm_rmit/rmit_main.rego): Service level agreements with third-party providers include regulator and institution access rights to records and decision minutes, prior notice of substantial sub-contracting, a secrecy undertaking surviving the engagement, disaster recovery and backup, uptime objectives, exit and termination continuity with timely data recovery, prompt disclosure of disruptions and cyber incidents in the provider's or sub-contractors' environment, compliance with international standards and staff certification, and participation in security awareness programmes

Evaluated by Rego package bnm_rmit.main (frameworks/financial/bnm_rmit/rmit_main.rego): A roadmap achieves continuous monitoring of third-party cybersecurity posture: measuring the infrastructure footprint and customer information accessible to third parties, leading product-specific controls, incident response protocols with providers for software-update vulnerabilities, a priority set of controls with frequent assurance assertions, higher-frequency monitoring of disclosed incidents, automated metric testing, and response to breached thresholds

Evaluated by Rego package bnm_rmit.main (frameworks/financial/bnm_rmit/rmit_main.rego): An SDLC methodology covers requirement, design, development, testing, deployment, change management, maintenance and decommissioning, integrated with enterprise architecture, risk management and security principles including segregation of duties

Evaluated by Rego package bnm_rmit.main (frameworks/financial/bnm_rmit/rmit_main.rego): A comprehensive risk assessment precedes cloud adoption, addressing deployment model sophistication, migration, infrastructure location and geopolitical and legal risk, multi-tenancy and data co-mingling, lock-in and portability, security configurability, exposure via the provider, termination and data recovery, demarcation of responsibilities and liability, and continuing regulatory and standards compliance

Evaluated by Rego package bnm_rmit.main (frameworks/financial/bnm_rmit/rmit_main.rego): Customer, counterparty and proprietary data on cloud services are safeguarded against unauthorised disclosure and access, with ownership, control and management of all such data and services retained, including cryptographic key management

Evaluated by Rego package bnm_rmit.main (frameworks/financial/bnm_rmit/rmit_main.rego): An access control policy governs identification, authentication and authorisation of all users to IT assets and data, with granularity commensurate with unauthorised-access risk

Evaluated by Rego package bnm_rmit.main (frameworks/financial/bnm_rmit/rmit_main.rego): Access control adheres to deny-all by default, least privilege on a need-to-have basis, time-bound access, segregation of incompatible functions (development vs operations, security vs system administration, network operation vs network security, IT operations), dual-authorisation criteria, and authentication by criticality: stronger for critical activities and remote access, robust identity verification at provisioning, and credentials uniquely linked to one user

Evaluated by Rego package bnm_rmit.main (frameworks/financial/bnm_rmit/rmit_main.rego): Multi-factor authentication resistant to social engineering, combining two or more of knowledge, inherent and possession factors, authenticates user access to critical systems

Evaluated by Rego package bnm_rmit.main (frameworks/financial/bnm_rmit/rmit_main.rego): A user access matrix outlines access rights, roles or profiles and the authorising and approving authorities, reviewed and updated periodically

Evaluated by Rego package bnm_rmit.main (frameworks/financial/bnm_rmit/rmit_main.rego): Access controls to enterprise-wide systems are managed and monitored, anomalies are flagged for prompt investigation, and user activities in critical systems are logged, retained at least three years and reviewed in a timely manner

Evaluated by Rego package bnm_rmit.main (frameworks/financial/bnm_rmit/rmit_main.rego): Rapid development (DevOps) meets enterprise security, governance and compliance requirements, with automated IT security compliance review and automated vulnerability discovery and testing before release

Evaluated by Rego package bnm_rmit.main (frameworks/financial/bnm_rmit/rmit_main.rego): Production is physically segregated from development and testing; on cloud, these environments do not run on the same virtual host

Evaluated by Rego package bnm_rmit.main (frameworks/financial/bnm_rmit/rmit_main.rego): Rigorous system testing precedes deployment, verifying user requirements and robustness; sensitive test data requires authorisation and disclosure safeguards

Evaluated by Rego package bnm_rmit.main (frameworks/financial/bnm_rmit/rmit_main.rego): Cyber risk management has an enterprise-wide focus reflecting the collective responsibility of business and technology lines

Evaluated by Rego package bnm_rmit.main (frameworks/financial/bnm_rmit/rmit_main.rego): A cyber threat intelligence process collects, analyses and evaluates threat information including data breaches and misleading information about the institution on the Internet, social media and dark web
Evaluated by Rego package bnm_rmit.main (frameworks/financial/bnm_rmit/rmit_main.rego): Flagged anomalous activities are investigated and responded to according to their complexity

Evaluated by Rego package bnm_rmit.main (frameworks/financial/bnm_rmit/rmit_main.rego): Cyber crisis management policies and procedures incorporate attack scenarios and responses into the crisis management plan, escalation, BCP and DR, with a communication plan for shareholders, regulators, customers and employees

Evaluated by Rego package bnm_rmit.main (frameworks/financial/bnm_rmit/rmit_main.rego): A Cyber Incident Response Plan covers preparedness (CERT governance, reporting, roles, invocation and escalation), detection and analysis (points of compromise, damage assessment including threat-actor claims, evidence preservation), containment and eradication, recovery with contingency strategies, and post-incident review with lessons learned
Evaluated by Rego package bnm_rmit.main (frameworks/financial/bnm_rmit/rmit_main.rego): CERT members are conversant with the incident response plan and procedures and remain contactable at all times

Evaluated by Rego package bnm_rmit.main (frameworks/financial/bnm_rmit/rmit_main.rego): A secure, reliable out-of-band communication infrastructure for internal and external stakeholders operates if primary communications are compromised

Evaluated by Rego package bnm_rmit.main (frameworks/financial/bnm_rmit/rmit_main.rego): An annual cyber drill tests the CIRP and out-of-band communications on current and emerging scenarios with the board, senior management and relevant third parties, covering escalation, communication and decision-making at different impact levels and the readiness of CERT and third parties; results are reported to the board

Evaluated by Rego package bnm_rmit.main (frameworks/financial/bnm_rmit/rmit_main.rego): Loss provision arrangements are reviewed against scenario analysis of extreme cyber events; any cyber insurance adequately covers the events and liabilities, its warranties and obligations are reflected in crisis procedures without unintended exclusions, and insurer obligations do not impair acting in the institution's and customers' best interests

Evaluated by Rego package bnm_rmit.main (frameworks/financial/bnm_rmit/rmit_main.rego): Cyber incidents are notified to the Bank per the Operational Risk Reporting, Business Continuity Management and Merchant Acquiring Services policy documents and any other specified policy

Evaluated by Rego package bnm_rmit.main (frameworks/financial/bnm_rmit/rmit_main.rego): Cyber threat intelligence is shared with the industry on a timely basis via the Bank's, industry's or law enforcement platforms, with resources allocated to industry-wide intelligence initiatives

Evaluated by Rego package bnm_rmit.main (frameworks/financial/bnm_rmit/rmit_main.rego): A cyber resilience framework (CRF) articulates governance, resilience objectives and risk tolerance against the evolving threat environment, targets operational resilience against extreme but plausible attacks, and supports identification, protection, detection, response and recovery of on-premises and third-party-hosted systems and data

Evaluated by Rego package bnm_rmit.main (frameworks/financial/bnm_rmit/rmit_main.rego): The institution collaborates and cooperates closely with relevant stakeholders and authorities in combating cyber threats

Evaluated by Rego package bnm_rmit.main (frameworks/financial/bnm_rmit/rmit_main.rego): The CRF includes institutional understanding of cyber risk context and posture; identification, classification and prioritisation of critical systems, information, assets and interconnectivity; threats, vulnerabilities and countermeasures; layered defence with zero-trust, micro-segmentation and security by design; continuous surveillance for timely detection; incident handling procedures and a crisis response playbook; secure information sharing with other institutions and FMIs; a centralised automated technology asset inventory; and a cyber risk management function escalating high-risk threats to senior management and the board

Evaluated by Rego package bnm_rmit.main (frameworks/financial/bnm_rmit/rmit_main.rego): As a designated National Critical Information Infrastructure entity, the institution complies with the Cyber Security Act 2024 requirements, guidelines and NACSA directives and standards
Evaluated by Rego package bnm_rmit.main (frameworks/financial/bnm_rmit/rmit_main.rego): The Appendix 5 control measures are adopted to enhance resilience to cyber attacks
Evaluated by Rego package bnm_rmit.main (frameworks/financial/bnm_rmit/rmit_main.rego): A realistic red-team simulation attack on the infrastructure is conducted at least once every three years

Evaluated by Rego package bnm_rmit.main (frameworks/financial/bnm_rmit/rmit_main.rego): Cybersecurity operations have clear responsibilities with mitigating measures for each phase of the attack life cycle: reconnaissance, weaponisation, delivery, exploitation, installation, command and control, exfiltration

Evaluated by Rego package bnm_rmit.main (frameworks/financial/bnm_rmit/rmit_main.rego): Continuous proactive monitoring and timely detection of anomalies via a Security Operations Centre with competent resources and tools, covering all critical systems and supporting infrastructure, with regular vulnerability assessment and penetration testing per Appendix 5

Evaluated by Rego package bnm_rmit.main (frameworks/financial/bnm_rmit/rmit_main.rego): The CRF implements robust security controls for digital services: minimum controls per delivery channel assessed regularly (Appendices 2, 3, 4, 11), proper user and device authentication and transaction authorisation against impersonation and fraud (Appendix 3), and strong physical and logical controls

Evaluated by Rego package bnm_rmit.main (frameworks/financial/bnm_rmit/rmit_main.rego): Where the §12 digital services controls are not yet implemented, documented explanation shows alternatives are at least as effective and the institution assumes liability for fraud arising from the gap

Evaluated by Rego package bnm_rmit.main (frameworks/financial/bnm_rmit/rmit_main.rego): The CRF extends to customers' mobile devices and access points: layered controls protecting the mobile application and its data, continuous surveillance of exploitation with swift control upgrades, incident handling to help customers contain damage, coordinated rapid countermeasure upgrades across functions, senior management review with escalation thresholds, and board apprisal of outcomes

Evaluated by Rego package bnm_rmit.main (frameworks/financial/bnm_rmit/rmit_main.rego): Fraud detection capabilities and rules are updated promptly on new modus operandi, supported by risk analytics and continuous upgrade per Appendix 11 Fraud Detection Standards

Evaluated by Rego package bnm_rmit.main (frameworks/financial/bnm_rmit/rmit_main.rego): Digital service delivery risks are mitigated: secure communication channels with compensating controls for phishing-prone channels (no clickable links in SMS), advance customer information on new controls, and practical ways for customers to verify calls from the institution or its outsourced providers

Evaluated by Rego package bnm_rmit.main (frameworks/financial/bnm_rmit/rmit_main.rego): Customers can manage activation and de-activation of payment cards for card-not-present and overseas transactions, without diminishing the institution's liabilities and duty of care

Evaluated by Rego package bnm_rmit.main (frameworks/financial/bnm_rmit/rmit_main.rego): Customer awareness programmes are continuously reviewed for effectiveness: timely practical fraud-identification information including new modus operandi, clear explanation of security measures and how to verify genuine sites and apps, real-time alerts when measures are absent, and measures such as interactive simulations

Evaluated by Rego package bnm_rmit.main (frameworks/financial/bnm_rmit/rmit_main.rego): Customers can conveniently report, suspend and re-activate accounts on suspected fraud: a secure self-service kill switch, an adequately resourced contact centre, and restoration of access within a reasonable time after validation

Evaluated by Rego package bnm_rmit.main (frameworks/financial/bnm_rmit/rmit_main.rego): Incidents involving potential fraud or compromised customer data trigger heightened monitoring of affected accounts, notification of affected customers with mitigation information, and revocation and re-issue of affected credentials or payment instruments where exploitation risk exists

Evaluated by Rego package bnm_rmit.main (frameworks/financial/bnm_rmit/rmit_main.rego): Scope, frequency and intensity of technology audits are commensurate with the complexity, sophistication and criticality of systems and applications

Evaluated by Rego package bnm_rmit.main (frameworks/financial/bnm_rmit/rmit_main.rego): The technology audit plan is reviewed annually with appropriate frequency and coverage of critical services, third-party providers, material external interfaces, delayed or terminated critical projects, and post-implementation reviews of new or material enhancements

Evaluated by Rego package bnm_rmit.main (frameworks/financial/bnm_rmit/rmit_main.rego): Internal audit has dedicated, specialised, professionally certified technology audit resources conversant with the institution's systems and delivery channels

Evaluated by Rego package bnm_rmit.main (frameworks/financial/bnm_rmit/rmit_main.rego): A technically competent external provider performs a production data centre resilience and risk assessment (DCRA) at least every three years or on material change, covering paragraphs 10.24–10.28; reliance on third-party reports for provider-managed data centres is consistent with risk appetite and meets the same requirements; the board-level committee deliberates the outcome

Evaluated by Rego package bnm_rmit.main (frameworks/financial/bnm_rmit/rmit_main.rego): A technically competent external provider performs network resilience and risk assessments (NRA) at least every three years or on material network design change, covering paragraphs 10.36–10.43; the board-level committee deliberates the outcome

Evaluated by Rego package bnm_rmit.main (frameworks/financial/bnm_rmit/rmit_main.rego): Regular technology and cybersecurity awareness education for all staff is conducted at least annually, reflects the evolving threat landscape, is measured for effectiveness, and includes third-party providers where appropriate

Evaluated by Rego package bnm_rmit.main (frameworks/financial/bnm_rmit/rmit_main.rego): Staff in technology operations, cybersecurity and risk management receive adequate continuous training and are competent and suitably certified

Evaluated by Rego package bnm_rmit.main (frameworks/financial/bnm_rmit/rmit_main.rego): Board members receive regular training and information on technology developments to discharge their oversight role

Evaluated by Rego package bnm_rmit.main (frameworks/financial/bnm_rmit/rmit_main.rego): The board establishes and approves a technology risk appetite aligned with the institution's risk appetite: risk tolerances for technology events, a risk owner and residual-risk acceptance criteria and authority, key risk indicators, sufficient resources, and regular review

Evaluated by Rego package bnm_rmit.main (frameworks/financial/bnm_rmit/rmit_main.rego): The board approves and reviews IT and cybersecurity strategic plans of at least three years, endorses and oversees the TRMF and CRF, requires robust risk assessments for critical systems and emerging technology, has IT frameworks and policies reviewed at least every three years, and ensures the framework supports technology applications to the Bank

Evaluated by Rego package bnm_rmit.main (frameworks/financial/bnm_rmit/rmit_main.rego): A board-level committee with at least one member with technology experience and competencies oversees technology matters

Evaluated by Rego package dora.rts_ict_risk (frameworks/financial/dora/dora_rts_ict_risk.rego): ensure the security of networks;
Evaluated by Rego package dora.rts_ict_risk (frameworks/financial/dora/dora_rts_ict_risk.rego): contain safeguards against intrusions and data misuse;

Evaluated by Rego package dora.rts_ict_risk (frameworks/financial/dora/dora_rts_ict_risk.rego): preserve the availability, authenticity, integrity, and confidentiality of data, including via the use of cryptographic techniques;
Evaluated by Rego package dora.rts_ict_risk (frameworks/financial/dora/dora_rts_ict_risk.rego): guarantee an accurate and prompt data transmission without major disruptions and undue delays.

Evaluated by Rego package dora.rts_ict_risk (frameworks/financial/dora/dora_rts_ict_risk.rego): are aligned to the financial entity’s information security objectives included in the digital operational resilience strategy referred to in Article 6(8) of Regulation (EU) 2022/2554;
Evaluated by Rego package dora.rts_ict_risk (frameworks/financial/dora/dora_rts_ict_risk.rego): indicate the date of the formal approval of the ICT security policies by the management body;

Evaluated by Rego package dora.rts_ict_risk (frameworks/financial/dora/dora_rts_ict_risk.rego): contain indicators and measures to: (i) monitor the implementation of the ICT security policies, procedures, protocols, and tools; (ii) record exceptions from that implementation; (iii) ensure that the digital operational resilience of the financial entity is ensured in case of exceptions as referred to in point (ii);
Evaluated by Rego package dora.rts_ict_risk (frameworks/financial/dora/dora_rts_ict_risk.rego): specify the responsibilities of staff at all levels to ensure the financial entity’s ICT security;

Evaluated by Rego package dora.rts_ict_risk (frameworks/financial/dora/dora_rts_ict_risk.rego): specify the consequences of non-compliance by staff of the financial entity with the ICT security policies, where provisions to that effect are not laid down in other policies of the financial entity;
Evaluated by Rego package dora.rts_ict_risk (frameworks/financial/dora/dora_rts_ict_risk.rego): list the documentation to be maintained;

Evaluated by Rego package dora.rts_ict_risk (frameworks/financial/dora/dora_rts_ict_risk.rego): specify the segregation of duties arrangements in the context of the three lines of defence model or other internal risk management and control model, as applicable, to avoid conflicts of interest;

Evaluated by Rego package dora.rts_ict_risk (frameworks/financial/dora/dora_rts_ict_risk.rego): consider leading practices and, where applicable, standards as defined in Article 2, point (1), of Regulation (EU) No 1025/2012;

Evaluated by Rego package dora.rts_ict_risk (frameworks/financial/dora/dora_rts_ict_risk.rego): identify the roles and responsibilities for the development, implementation and maintenance of ICT security policies, procedures, protocols, and tools;
Evaluated by Rego package dora.rts_ict_risk (frameworks/financial/dora/dora_rts_ict_risk.rego): are reviewed in accordance with Article 6(5) of Regulation (EU) 2022/2554;

Evaluated by Rego package dora.rts_ict_risk (frameworks/financial/dora/dora_rts_ict_risk.rego): take into account material changes concerning the financial entity, including material changes to the activities or processes of the financial entity, to the cyber threat landscape, or to applicable legal obligations.

Evaluated by Rego package dora.rts_ict_risk (frameworks/financial/dora/dora_rts_ict_risk.rego): an indication of the approval of the risk tolerance level for ICT risk established in accordance with Article 6(8), point (b), of Regulation (EU) 2022/2554;

Evaluated by Rego package dora.rts_ict_risk (frameworks/financial/dora/dora_rts_ict_risk.rego): a procedure and a methodology to conduct the ICT risk assessment, identifying: (i) vulnerabilities and threats that affect or may affect the supported business functions, the ICT systems and ICT assets supporting those functions; (ii) the quantitative or qualitative indicators to measure the impact and likelihood of the vulnerabilities and threats referred to in point (i);

Evaluated by Rego package dora.rts_ict_risk (frameworks/financial/dora/dora_rts_ict_risk.rego): the procedure to identify, implement, and document ICT risk treatment measures for the ICT risks identified and assessed, including the determination of ICT risk treatment measures necessary to bring ICT risk within the risk tolerance level referred to in point (a); [Second subparagraph:] For the purposes of the first paragraph, point (c), the procedure referred to in that point shall ensure: (a) the monitoring of the effectiveness of the ICT risk treatment measures implemented; (b) the assessment of whether the established risk tolerance levels of the financial entity have been attained; (c) the assessment of whether the financial entity has taken actions to correct or improve those measures where necessary.

Evaluated by Rego package dora.rts_ict_risk (frameworks/financial/dora/dora_rts_ict_risk.rego): for the residual ICT risks that are still present following the implementation of the ICT risk treatment measures referred to in point (c): (i) provisions on the identification of those residual ICT risks; (ii) the assignment of roles and responsibilities regarding: (1) the acceptance of the residual ICT risks that exceed the financial entity’s risk tolerance level referred to in point (a); (2) for the review process referred to in point (iv) of this point (d); (iii) the development of an inventory of the accepted residual ICT risks, including a justification for their acceptance; (iv) provisions on the review of the accepted residual ICT risks at least once a year, including: (1) the identification of any changes to the residual ICT risks; (2) the assessment of available mitigation measures; (3) the assessment of whether the reasons justifying the acceptance of residual ICT risks are still valid and applicable at the date of the review;

Evaluated by Rego package dora.rts_ict_risk (frameworks/financial/dora/dora_rts_ict_risk.rego): provisions on the monitoring of: (i) any changes to the ICT risk and cyber threat landscape; (ii) internal and external vulnerabilities and threats: (iii) ICT risk of the financial entity that enables promp detection of changes that could affect its ICT risk profile;

Evaluated by Rego package dora.rts_ict_risk (frameworks/financial/dora/dora_rts_ict_risk.rego): provisions on a process to ensure that any changes to the business strategy and the digital operational resilience strategy of the financial entity are taken into account.

Evaluated by Rego package dora.rts_ict_risk (frameworks/financial/dora/dora_rts_ict_risk.rego): As part of the ICT security policies, procedures, protocols, and tools referred to in Article 9(2) of Regulation (EU) 2022/2554, financial entities shall develop, document, and implement a policy on management of ICT assets.

Evaluated by Rego package dora.rts_ict_risk (frameworks/financial/dora/dora_rts_ict_risk.rego): prescribe the monitoring and management of the lifecycle of ICT assets identified and classified in accordance with Article 8(1) of Regulation (EU) 2022/2554;

Evaluated by Rego package dora.rts_ict_risk (frameworks/financial/dora/dora_rts_ict_risk.rego): prescribe that the financial entity keeps records of all of the following: (i) the unique identifier of each ICT asset; (ii) information on the location, either physical or logical, of all ICT assets; (iii) the classification of all ICT assets, as referred to in Article 8(1) of Regulation (EU) 2022/2254; (iv) the identity of ICT asset owners; (v) the business functions or services supported by the ICT asset; (vi) the ICT business continuity requirements, including recovery time objectives and recovery point objectives; (vii) whether the ICT asset can be or is exposed to external networks, including the internet; (viii) the links and interdependencies among ICT assets and the business functions using each ICT asset; (ix) where applicable, for all ICT assets, the end dates of the ICT third-party service provider’s regular, extended, and custom support services after which those ICT assets are no longer supported by their supplier or by an ICT third-party service provider;

Evaluated by Rego package dora.rts_ict_risk (frameworks/financial/dora/dora_rts_ict_risk.rego): for financial entities other than microenterprises, prescribe that those financial entities keep records of the information necessary to perform a specific ICT risk assessment on all legacy ICT systems referred to in Article 8(7) of Regulation (EU) 2022/2554.
Evaluated by Rego package dora.rts_ict_risk (frameworks/financial/dora/dora_rts_ict_risk.rego): Financial entities shall develop, document, and implement a procedure for the management of ICT assets.

Evaluated by Rego package dora.rts_ict_risk (frameworks/financial/dora/dora_rts_ict_risk.rego): the ICT risk related to those business functions and their dependencies on the information assets or ICT assets;

Evaluated by Rego package dora.rts_ict_risk (frameworks/financial/dora/dora_rts_ict_risk.rego): how the loss of confidentiality, integrity, and availability of such information assets and ICT assets would impact the business processes and activities of the financial entities.

Evaluated by Rego package dora.rts_ict_risk (frameworks/financial/dora/dora_rts_ict_risk.rego): As part of their ICT security policies, procedures, protocols, and tools referred to in Article 9(2) of Regulation (EU) 2022/2554, financial entities shall develop, document, and implement a policy on encryption and cryptographic controls.
Evaluated by Rego package dora.rts_ict_risk (frameworks/financial/dora/dora_rts_ict_risk.rego): the encryption of data at rest and in transit;

Evaluated by Rego package dora.rts_ict_risk (frameworks/financial/dora/dora_rts_ict_risk.rego): the encryption of data in use, where necessary; [Second subparagraph:] For the purposes of point (b), where encryption of data in use is not possible, financial entities shall process data in use in a separated and protected environment, or take equivalent measures to ensure the confidentiality, integrity, authenticity, and availability of data.
Evaluated by Rego package dora.rts_ict_risk (frameworks/financial/dora/dora_rts_ict_risk.rego): the encryption of internal network connections and traffic with external parties;

Evaluated by Rego package dora.rts_ict_risk (frameworks/financial/dora/dora_rts_ict_risk.rego): the cryptographic key management referred to in Article 7, laying down rules on the correct use, protection, and lifecycle of cryptographic keys.

Evaluated by Rego package dora.rts_ict_risk (frameworks/financial/dora/dora_rts_ict_risk.rego): Financial entities shall include in the policy on encryption and cryptographic controls referred to in paragraph 1 criteria for the selection of cryptographic techniques and use practices, taking into account leading practices, and standards as defined in Article 2, point (1), of Regulation (EU) No 1025/2012, and the classification of relevant ICT assets established in accordance with Article 8(1) of Regulation (EU) 2022/2554. Financial entities that are not able to adhere to the leading practices or standards, or to use the most reliable techniques, shall adopt mitigation and monitoring measures that ensure resilience against cyber threats.

Evaluated by Rego package dora.rts_ict_risk (frameworks/financial/dora/dora_rts_ict_risk.rego): Financial entities shall include in the policy on encryption and cryptographic controls referred to in paragraph 1 provisions for updating or changing, where necessary, the cryptographic technology on the basis of developments in cryptanalysis. Those updates or changes shall ensure that the cryptographic technology remains resilient against cyber threats, as required by Article 10(2), point (a). Financial entities that are not able to update or change the cryptographic technology shall adopt mitigation and monitoring measures that ensure resilience against cyber threats.

Evaluated by Rego package dora.rts_ict_risk (frameworks/financial/dora/dora_rts_ict_risk.rego): Financial entities shall include in the policy on encryption and cryptographic controls referred to in paragraph 1 a requirement to record the adoption of mitigation and monitoring measures adopted in accordance with paragraphs 3 and 4 and to provide a reasoned explanation for doing so.

Evaluated by Rego package dora.rts_ict_risk (frameworks/financial/dora/dora_rts_ict_risk.rego): Financial entities shall include in the cryptographic key management policy referred to in Article 6(2), point (d), requirements for managing cryptographic keys through their whole lifecycle, including generating, renewing, storing, backing up, archiving, retrieving, transmitting, retiring, revoking, and destroying those cryptographic keys.

Evaluated by Rego package dora.rts_ict_risk (frameworks/financial/dora/dora_rts_ict_risk.rego): Financial entities shall identify and implement controls to protect cryptographic keys through their whole lifecycle against loss, unauthorised access, disclosure, and modification. Financial entities shall design those controls on the basis of the results of the approved data classification and the ICT risk assessment.

Evaluated by Rego package dora.rts_ict_risk (frameworks/financial/dora/dora_rts_ict_risk.rego): Financial entities shall develop and implement methods to replace the cryptographic keys in the case of loss, or where those keys are compromised or damaged.

Evaluated by Rego package dora.rts_ict_risk (frameworks/financial/dora/dora_rts_ict_risk.rego): Financial entities shall create and maintain a register for all certificates and certificate-storing devices for at least ICT assets supporting critical or important functions. Financial entities shall keep that register up to date.
Evaluated by Rego package dora.rts_ict_risk (frameworks/financial/dora/dora_rts_ict_risk.rego): Financial entities shall ensure the prompt renewal of certificates in advance of their expiration.

Evaluated by Rego package dora.rts_ict_risk (frameworks/financial/dora/dora_rts_ict_risk.rego): As part of the ICT security policies, procedures, protocols, and tools referred to in Article 9(2) of Regulation (EU) 2022/2554, financial entities shall develop, document, and implement policies and procedures to manage the ICT operations. Those policies and procedures shall specify how financial entities operate, monitor, control, and restore their ICT assets, including the documentation of ICT operations.

Evaluated by Rego package dora.rts_ict_risk (frameworks/financial/dora/dora_rts_ict_risk.rego): an ICT assets description, including all of the following: (i) requirements regarding secure installation, maintenance, configuration, and deinstallation of an ICT system; (ii) requirements regarding the management of information assets used by ICT assets, including their processing and handling, both automated and manual; (iii) requirements regarding the identification and control of legacy ICT systems;

Evaluated by Rego package dora.rts_ict_risk (frameworks/financial/dora/dora_rts_ict_risk.rego): controls and monitoring of ICT systems, including all of the following: (i) backup and restore requirements of ICT systems; (ii) scheduling requirements, taking into consideration interdependencies among the ICT systems; (iii) protocols for audit-trail and system log information; (iv) requirements to ensure that the performance of internal audit and other testing minimises disruptions to business operations; (v) requirements on the separation of ICT production environments from the development, testing, and other non-production environments; (vi) requirements to conduct the development and testing in environments which are separated from the production environment; (vii) requirements to conduct the development and testing in production environments; [Second subparagraph:] For the purposes of point (b)(v), the separation shall consider all of the components of the environment, including accounts, data or connections, as required by Article 13, first subparagraph, point (a). [Third subparagraph:] For the purposes of point (b)(vii), the policies and procedures referred to in paragraph 1 shall provide that the instances in which testing is performed in a production environment are clearly identified, reasoned, are for limited periods of time, and are approved by the relevant function in accordance with Article 16(6). Financial entities shall ensure the availability, confidentiality, integrity, and authenticity of ICT systems and production data during development and test activities in the production environment.

Evaluated by Rego package dora.rts_ict_risk (frameworks/financial/dora/dora_rts_ict_risk.rego): error handling concerning ICT systems, including all of the following: (i) procedures and protocols for handling errors; (ii) support and escalation contacts, including external support contacts in case of unexpected operational or technical issues; (iii) ICT system restart, rollback, and recovery procedures for use in the event of ICT system disruption.
Evaluated by Rego package dora.rts_ict_risk (frameworks/financial/dora/dora_rts_ict_risk.rego): the identification of capacity requirements of their ICT systems;
Evaluated by Rego package dora.rts_ict_risk (frameworks/financial/dora/dora_rts_ict_risk.rego): the application of resource optimisation;

Evaluated by Rego package dora.rts_ict_risk (frameworks/financial/dora/dora_rts_ict_risk.rego): the monitoring procedures for maintaining and improving: (i) the availability of data and ICT systems; (ii) the efficiency of ICT systems; (iii) the prevention of ICT capacity shortages.

Evaluated by Rego package dora.rts_ict_risk (frameworks/financial/dora/dora_rts_ict_risk.rego): The capacity and performance management procedures referred to in paragraph 1 shall ensure that financial entities take measures that are appropriate to cater for the specificities of ICT systems with long or complex procurement or approval processes or ICT systems that are resource-intensive.

Evaluated by Rego package dora.rts_ict_risk (frameworks/financial/dora/dora_rts_ict_risk.rego): As part of the ICT security policies, procedures, protocols, and tools referred to in Article 9(2) of Regulation (EU) 2022/2554, financial entities shall develop, document, and implement vulnerability management procedures.

Evaluated by Rego package dora.rts_ict_risk (frameworks/financial/dora/dora_rts_ict_risk.rego): identify and update relevant and trustworthy information resources to build and maintain awareness about vulnerabilities;

Evaluated by Rego package dora.rts_ict_risk (frameworks/financial/dora/dora_rts_ict_risk.rego): ensure the performance of automated vulnerability scanning and assessments on ICT assets, whereby the frequency and scope of those activities shall be commensurate to the classification established in accordance with Article 8(1) of Regulation (EU) 2022/2554 and the overall risk profile of the ICT asset; [Second subparagraph:] For the purposes of point (b), financial entities shall perform the automated vulnerability scanning and assessments on ICT assets for the ICT assets supporting critical or important functions on at least a weekly basis.

Evaluated by Rego package dora.rts_ict_risk (frameworks/financial/dora/dora_rts_ict_risk.rego): verify whether: (i) ICT third-party service providers handle vulnerabilities related to the ICT services provided to the financial entity; (ii) whether those service providers report to the financial entity at least the critical vulnerabilities and statistics and trends in a timely manner; [Third subparagraph:] For the purposes of point (c), financial entities shall request that ICT third-party service providers investigate the relevant vulnerabilities, determine the root causes, and implement appropriate mitigating action.

Evaluated by Rego package dora.rts_ict_risk (frameworks/financial/dora/dora_rts_ict_risk.rego): track the usage of: (i) third-party libraries, including open-source libraries, used by ICT services supporting critical or important functions; (ii) ICT services developed by the financial entity itself or specifically customised or developed for the financial entity by an ICT third-party service provider; [Fourth subparagraph:] For the purposes of point (d), financial entities shall, where appropriate in collaboration with the ICT third-party service provider, monitor the version and possible updates of the third-party libraries. In case of ready to use (off-the-shelf) ICT assets or components of ICT assets acquired and used in the operation of ICT services not supporting critical or important functions, financial entities shall track the usage to the extent possible of third-party libraries, including open-source libraries.

Evaluated by Rego package dora.rts_ict_risk (frameworks/financial/dora/dora_rts_ict_risk.rego): establish procedures for the responsible disclosure of vulnerabilities to clients, counterparties, and to the public;

Evaluated by Rego package dora.rts_ict_risk (frameworks/financial/dora/dora_rts_ict_risk.rego): prioritise the deployment of patches and other mitigation measures to address the vulnerabilities identified; [Fifth subparagraph:] For the purposes of point (f), financial entities shall consider the criticality of the vulnerability, the classification established in accordance with Article 8(1) of Regulation (EU) 2022/2554, and the risk profile of the ICT assets affected by the identified vulnerabilities.
Evaluated by Rego package dora.rts_ict_risk (frameworks/financial/dora/dora_rts_ict_risk.rego): monitor and verify the remediation of vulnerabilities;

Evaluated by Rego package dora.rts_ict_risk (frameworks/financial/dora/dora_rts_ict_risk.rego): require the recording of any detected vulnerabilities affecting ICT systems and the monitoring of their resolution.

Evaluated by Rego package dora.rts_ict_risk (frameworks/financial/dora/dora_rts_ict_risk.rego): As part of the ICT security policies, procedures, protocols, and tools referred to in Article 9(2) of Regulation (EU) 2022/2554, financial entities shall develop, document and implement patch management procedures.

Evaluated by Rego package dora.rts_ict_risk (frameworks/financial/dora/dora_rts_ict_risk.rego): to the extent possible identify and evaluate available software and hardware patches and updates using automated tools;
Evaluated by Rego package dora.rts_ict_risk (frameworks/financial/dora/dora_rts_ict_risk.rego): identify emergency procedures for the patching and updating of ICT assets;

Evaluated by Rego package dora.rts_ict_risk (frameworks/financial/dora/dora_rts_ict_risk.rego): test and deploy the software and hardware patches and the updates referred to in Article 8(2), points (b)(v), (vi) and (vii);

Evaluated by Rego package dora.rts_ict_risk (frameworks/financial/dora/dora_rts_ict_risk.rego): set deadlines for the installation of software and hardware patches and updates and escalation procedures in case those deadlines cannot be met.

Evaluated by Rego package dora.rts_ict_risk (frameworks/financial/dora/dora_rts_ict_risk.rego): As part of the ICT security policies, procedures, protocols, and tools referred to in Article 9(2) of Regulation (EU) 2022/2554, financial entities shall develop, document, and implement a data and system security procedure.

Evaluated by Rego package dora.rts_ict_risk (frameworks/financial/dora/dora_rts_ict_risk.rego): the access restrictions referred to in Article 21 of this Regulation, supporting the protection requirements for each level of classification;
