Evaluated by Rego package hkma_trm.main (frameworks/financial/hkma_trm/hkma_trm_main.rego): IT control policies setting the ground rules for IT controls are developed by senior management, formally approved by the Board or its committee, and implemented across IT functions and business units

Evaluated by Rego package hkma_trm.main (frameworks/financial/hkma_trm/hkma_trm_main.rego): IT control policies cover at least security management, system development and change management, information processing, communications networks and service providers, and are reviewed regularly and updated

Evaluated by Rego package hkma_trm.main (frameworks/financial/hkma_trm/hkma_trm_main.rego): Processes to verify compliance with IT control policies and to seek approval for dispensation are specified, with defined consequences for non-adherence

Evaluated by Rego package hkma_trm.main (frameworks/financial/hkma_trm/hkma_trm_main.rego): Mechanisms (periodic reminders, orientation for new recruits) promote regular awareness of IT control policies

Evaluated by Rego package hkma_trm.main (frameworks/financial/hkma_trm/hkma_trm_main.rego): An IT organisation structure and job descriptions for IT functions are documented and approved by senior management

Evaluated by Rego package hkma_trm.main (frameworks/financial/hkma_trm/hkma_trm_main.rego): Segregation of duties within and among IT functions is enforced (developers have no production access; security management has no conflicting duties), with compensating controls such as peer review where segregation is impractical

Evaluated by Rego package hkma_trm.main (frameworks/financial/hkma_trm/hkma_trm_main.rego): An IT planning or steering committee of senior management, business units and IT meets regularly and reports major technology initiatives and material IT issues to senior management and the Board

Evaluated by Rego package hkma_trm.main (frameworks/financial/hkma_trm/hkma_trm_main.rego): A documented IT strategy covering long- and short-term initiatives is endorsed by the Board and senior management and reviewed at least annually
Evaluated by Rego package hkma_trm.main (frameworks/financial/hkma_trm/hkma_trm_main.rego): The function responsible for the technology risk management (TRM) process is clearly established

Evaluated by Rego package hkma_trm.main (frameworks/financial/hkma_trm/hkma_trm_main.rego): The TRM function assists business units and IT in identifying, measuring, monitoring and controlling technology risks, promotes policy compliance and supports investigation of technology-related frauds and incidents

Evaluated by Rego package hkma_trm.main (frameworks/financial/hkma_trm/hkma_trm_main.rego): A formal technology risk acknowledgement and acceptance process reviews, evaluates and approves major non-compliance with IT control policies: risk description and assessment, mitigating controls, remedial plan, approval by the risk owner and senior management

Evaluated by Rego package hkma_trm.main (frameworks/financial/hkma_trm/hkma_trm_main.rego): Technology audits periodically assess the TRM process and IT controls under an annual technology audit plan; audit issues are recorded, followed up and rectified

Evaluated by Rego package hkma_trm.main (frameworks/financial/hkma_trm/hkma_trm_main.rego): Where in-house technology audit expertise is insufficient it is supplemented by external specialists or group technology auditors

Evaluated by Rego package hkma_trm.main (frameworks/financial/hkma_trm/hkma_trm_main.rego): Staff of IT functions, the TRM function and technology audit are competent, with sufficient staffing for present and expected demand and turnover

Evaluated by Rego package hkma_trm.main (frameworks/financial/hkma_trm/hkma_trm_main.rego): A process identifies material skill gaps against a skill matrix and an adequate training programme is in place; professional qualifications are encouraged for security, TRM and audit staff

Evaluated by Rego package hkma_trm.main (frameworks/financial/hkma_trm/hkma_trm_main.rego): Respective responsibilities of local and overseas offices for IT controls and support are clearly set out in policies, procedures or service agreements

Evaluated by Rego package hkma_trm.main (frameworks/financial/hkma_trm/hkma_trm_main.rego): Each application system has an assigned information owner accountable for confidentiality and integrity, working with the TRM and IT functions

Evaluated by Rego package hkma_trm.main (frameworks/financial/hkma_trm/hkma_trm_main.rego): Information is classified by sensitivity with guidelines, definitions and protection procedures for each class

Evaluated by Rego package hkma_trm.main (frameworks/financial/hkma_trm/hkma_trm_main.rego): Confidentiality is protected regardless of media; secure disposal and destruction processes exist for sensitive paper and electronic media

Evaluated by Rego package hkma_trm.main (frameworks/financial/hkma_trm/hkma_trm_main.rego): Cryptography uses industry-accepted solutions with sound key management: secure generation, distribution, storage, entry, use and archiving (tamper-resistant storage recommended) and off-site backup of keys under equivalent controls

Evaluated by Rego package hkma_trm.main (frameworks/financial/hkma_trm/hkma_trm_main.rego): Access to information and application systems is restricted by authentication and access control rules; every user has a unique ID with an appropriate authentication method

Evaluated by Rego package hkma_trm.main (frameworks/financial/hkma_trm/hkma_trm_main.rego): Effective password rules avoid easy-to-guess passwords and enforce periodic change; multi-factor authentication is used for higher-risk transactions and activities (payments, financial messages, mobile computing)

Evaluated by Rego package hkma_trm.main (frameworks/financial/hkma_trm/hkma_trm_main.rego): Privileged and emergency IDs are granted only necessary authorities, formally approved before release, monitored (peer review of logs), safeguarded, and have passwords changed immediately on return

Evaluated by Rego package hkma_trm.main (frameworks/financial/hkma_trm/hkma_trm_main.rego): A security administration function grants, changes and removes access with information-owner approval, removes rights on leaving or role change, re-certifies user access periodically (e.g. annually), reviews security logs and violation reports timely, and performs incident analysis, reporting and investigation

Evaluated by Rego package hkma_trm.main (frameworks/financial/hkma_trm/hkma_trm_main.rego): Segregation of duties or compensating controls within the security administration function mitigate unauthorised activity by that function

Evaluated by Rego package hkma_trm.main (frameworks/financial/hkma_trm/hkma_trm_main.rego): Incident response and reporting procedures handle security incidents during and outside office hours and include timely reporting to the HKMA of confirmed IT-related fraud or major security breaches

Evaluated by Rego package hkma_trm.main (frameworks/financial/hkma_trm/hkma_trm_main.rego): Baseline security requirements safeguard applications, operating systems, system software and databases: authenticated and authorised access, periodic static-data integrity checks, secure configuration with unnecessary services removed, timely vendor patching with clear responsibility, documented configurations with periodic certification, and protected logging and monitoring of system and user activity

Evaluated by Rego package hkma_trm.main (frameworks/financial/hkma_trm/hkma_trm_main.rego): End-user computing is controlled: data security, documentation, storage and backup, recovery, audit responsibilities and training

Evaluated by Rego package hkma_trm.main (frameworks/financial/hkma_trm/hkma_trm_main.rego): Mobile computing controls cover user approval, remote-access authentication, protection of devices against theft and malware, encryption of sensitive data in the mobile environment and in transit, and backup of mobile data

Evaluated by Rego package hkma_trm.main (frameworks/financial/hkma_trm/hkma_trm_main.rego): Malicious-software controls prohibit unauthorised downloads and doubtful sites, keep reputable anti-virus current, block executables and mobile code with known vulnerabilities, and scan all devices regularly with recovery procedures

Evaluated by Rego package hkma_trm.main (frameworks/financial/hkma_trm/hkma_trm_main.rego): Critical information processing facilities sit in secure areas with security barriers and entry controls; access is restricted to authorised personnel and reviewed regularly; buildings give minimum indication of purpose

Evaluated by Rego package hkma_trm.main (frameworks/financial/hkma_trm/hkma_trm_main.rego): Data centre sites consider environmental threats; environmental monitoring (fire, smoke, temperature, water, dust) and protection from power failure (UPS, backup generator) are in place

Evaluated by Rego package hkma_trm.main (frameworks/financial/hkma_trm/hkma_trm_main.rego): Third-party access to secure areas is approved and monitored; recruitment of permanent and temporary technology staff and contractors includes verification and background checks

Evaluated by Rego package hkma_trm.main (frameworks/financial/hkma_trm/hkma_trm_main.rego): A project management framework specifies the methodology for major technology projects: responsibilities, activity breakdown, time and resource budgets, milestones, checkpoints, dependencies, quality assurance, risk assessment and approvals

Evaluated by Rego package hkma_trm.main (frameworks/financial/hkma_trm/hkma_trm_main.rego): A full project life-cycle methodology governs development, implementation and maintenance of major systems from initiation through feasibility, requirements, design, development, testing, training, implementation, operation and maintenance

Evaluated by Rego package hkma_trm.main (frameworks/financial/hkma_trm/hkma_trm_main.rego): The life-cycle methodology defines roles and deliverables per phase and ensures security requirements are identified with business requirements, built, tested and implemented

Evaluated by Rego package hkma_trm.main (frameworks/financial/hkma_trm/hkma_trm_main.rego): An independent party (QA, TRM or technology audit) conducts a quality assurance review of major projects for compliance with the methodology, policies, control requirements, regulations and law

Evaluated by Rego package hkma_trm.main (frameworks/financial/hkma_trm/hkma_trm_main.rego): A formal acceptance process promotes only tested and approved systems to production; testing is in a separate environment; production data is not used in testing unless de-sensitised and approved by the information owner; performance testing precedes promotion

Evaluated by Rego package hkma_trm.main (frameworks/financial/hkma_trm/hkma_trm_main.rego): A formal software package acquisition process evaluates the package (licence, functionality, performance, security) and the supplier (financial condition, reputation, technical capability)

Evaluated by Rego package hkma_trm.main (frameworks/financial/hkma_trm/hkma_trm_main.rego): Ongoing maintenance and support of software packages are specified in formal contracts; escrow is considered for mission-critical packages

Evaluated by Rego package hkma_trm.main (frameworks/financial/hkma_trm/hkma_trm_main.rego): A formal change management process covers classification and impact, roles with segregation of duties so no one person can change production unreviewed, version control and audit trails, scheduling and tracking, rollback, and post-implementation verification

Evaluated by Rego package hkma_trm.main (frameworks/financial/hkma_trm/hkma_trm_main.rego): Emergency changes follow formal procedures and are approved by the information owner and relevant parties at the time, or endorsed by the information owner as soon as practicable afterwards

Evaluated by Rego package hkma_trm.main (frameworks/financial/hkma_trm/hkma_trm_main.rego): Emergency changes are logged and backed up (previous and changed versions and data), reviewed by independent personnel, and replaced by proper fixes through normal change management

Evaluated by Rego package hkma_trm.main (frameworks/financial/hkma_trm/hkma_trm_main.rego): Service level agreements with business units cover availability, performance, capacity for growth and user support, with procedures to manage delivery

Evaluated by Rego package hkma_trm.main (frameworks/financial/hkma_trm/hkma_trm_main.rego): An IT operations manual documents operator tasks, job scheduling and execution, and on-site and off-site backup of data and software (frequency, scope, retention) for production and development

Evaluated by Rego package hkma_trm.main (frameworks/financial/hkma_trm/hkma_trm_main.rego): A problem management system responds to IT operational incidents, escalates to IT management, and records, analyses and tracks incidents to rectification; a helpdesk provides front-line support

Evaluated by Rego package hkma_trm.main (frameworks/financial/hkma_trm/hkma_trm_main.rego): Application performance is continuously monitored with timely exception reporting and forecasting to identify problems early and feed capacity planning
Evaluated by Rego package hkma_trm.main (frameworks/financial/hkma_trm/hkma_trm_main.rego): Capacity planning covers backup systems and related facilities as well as production

Evaluated by Rego package hkma_trm.main (frameworks/financial/hkma_trm/hkma_trm_main.rego): IT facilities and equipment are maintained per industry practice and supplier intervals, with fault and maintenance records and a hardware and facility inventory of purchased and leased assets

Evaluated by Rego package hkma_trm.main (frameworks/financial/hkma_trm/hkma_trm_main.rego): An IT disaster recovery plan ensures critical application systems and technology services resume per business recovery requirements (TM-G-2), with adequate insurance of IT resources

Evaluated by Rego package hkma_trm.main (frameworks/financial/hkma_trm/hkma_trm_main.rego): Network management responsibility is assigned to skilled, resourced individuals; network standards, design, diagrams and procedures are documented, current, communicated and reviewed periodically

Evaluated by Rego package hkma_trm.main (frameworks/financial/hkma_trm/hkma_trm_main.rego): Critical communications facilities are identified and single points of failure minimised by automatic re-routing, multiple exchanges and alternate telecommunications providers

Evaluated by Rego package hkma_trm.main (frameworks/financial/hkma_trm/hkma_trm_main.rego): The network is monitored continuously: services and performance against targets, traffic volumes and bottlenecks, and detection of unusual activity based on attack characteristics

Evaluated by Rego package hkma_trm.main (frameworks/financial/hkma_trm/hkma_trm_main.rego): Powerful network analysis and monitoring tools are protected from unauthorised use and restricted to authorised staff under approval and review

Evaluated by Rego package hkma_trm.main (frameworks/financial/hkma_trm/hkma_trm_main.rego): Procedures for use of networks and network services define available services, authorisation of who may access them, and protection of access points, connections and services

Evaluated by Rego package hkma_trm.main (frameworks/financial/hkma_trm/hkma_trm_main.rego): Internal networks are segregated by access-control need; production systems sit in dedicated segments separated from internet, extranet and market-data traffic; sensitive inter-segment traffic is controlled and tamper-protected

Evaluated by Rego package hkma_trm.main (frameworks/financial/hkma_trm/hkma_trm_main.rego): Security parameter settings of routers, firewalls and network servers are reviewed regularly; audit trails of critical network devices are maintained and reviewed; operations staff are alerted in real time to potential breaches

Evaluated by Rego package hkma_trm.main (frameworks/financial/hkma_trm/hkma_trm_main.rego): Network certification assesses LAN/WAN additions or changes (dial ports, switches, terminal servers, gateways, routers, extranets, internet) for vulnerabilities and documents approval or required controls

Evaluated by Rego package hkma_trm.main (frameworks/financial/hkma_trm/hkma_trm_main.rego): WLAN policies cover approval, installation, operation and administration; a risk assessment of accessible information precedes implementation; a standard WLAN security configuration and network certification apply

Evaluated by Rego package hkma_trm.main (frameworks/financial/hkma_trm/hkma_trm_main.rego): Stronger encryption and mutual authentication protect wireless-to-wired traffic where needed; WLANs are segregated from the corporate network (e.g. firewalls)

Evaluated by Rego package hkma_trm.main (frameworks/financial/hkma_trm/hkma_trm_main.rego): Technology outsourcing follows SA-2 plus: providers have resources and expertise to meet IT control policies; critical services get an independent assessment of the provider's IT control environment with the report provided to the HKMA; agreements specify performance standards, obligations, ownership and sub-contracting notification or approval; an annual assessment confirms the control environment of critical providers; excessive reliance on a single provider is avoided; a contingency and exit plan exists for critical outsourced services

Evaluated by Rego package hkma_trm.main (frameworks/financial/hkma_trm/hkma_trm_main.rego): Guidelines govern other major technology service providers (telecommunications, network operators): selection, approval of material exceptions and avoidance of over-reliance on a single provider for critical services

Evaluated by Rego package hkma_trm.main (frameworks/financial/hkma_trm/hkma_trm_main.rego): A technology and cyber risk management framework proportionate to the nature, scale and complexity of operations is in place, consistent with IC-1 and TM-G-1

Evaluated by Rego package hkma_trm.main (frameworks/financial/hkma_trm/hkma_trm_main.rego): Significant cyber incidents are reported promptly to the HKMA and, where appropriate, other relevant authorities (e.g. PCPD, CSTCB) under prevailing legal and regulatory obligations

Evaluated by Rego package hkma_trm.main (frameworks/financial/hkma_trm/hkma_trm_main.rego): Regular Cyber Resilience Assessment Framework (C-RAF) assessments are conducted — inherent risk assessment, maturity assessment, and iCAST for medium or high inherent risk — raising cyber defence maturity to the assessed exposure

Evaluated by Rego package hkma_trm.main (frameworks/financial/hkma_trm/hkma_trm_main.rego): Secure Tertiary Data Backup (STDB) is adopted so critical data can be recovered if a cyber attack compromises both production and backup environments

Evaluated by Rego package hkma_trm.main (frameworks/financial/hkma_trm/hkma_trm_main.rego): The AI exchanges cyber threat intelligence through the Cyber Intelligence Sharing Platform (CISP) under the Cybersecurity Fortification Initiative

control-implementations.description: Controls of iec_62443 evaluated by the Rego Policy Libraries (130 controls, 12 Rego modules).

implemented-requirements.description: Evaluated by Rego package iec_62443.fr1 (frameworks/critical_infrastructure/iec_62443/fr1_identification_authentication.rego): evidence missing - input.target_sl not provided; Security Level dependent requirements cannot be evaluated

Evaluated by Rego package iec_62443.fr1 (frameworks/critical_infrastructure/iec_62443/fr1_identification_authentication.rego): ICS system '%v' does not enforce unique user identification. Every human user must have a unique identifier.

Evaluated by Rego package iec_62443.fr1 (frameworks/critical_infrastructure/iec_62443/fr1_identification_authentication.rego): IEC 62443 SR 1.1 RE 1 SL%v (IAC): ICS system '%v' does not enforce multi-factor authentication. MFA is required at Security Level 2+.

Evaluated by Rego package iec_62443.fr1 (frameworks/critical_infrastructure/iec_62443/fr1_identification_authentication.rego): IEC 62443 SR 1.1 RE 2 SL%v (IAC): Hardware token-based authentication is not implemented. Required at Security Level 3+.

Evaluated by Rego package iec_62443.fr1 (frameworks/critical_infrastructure/iec_62443/fr1_identification_authentication.rego): ICS system '%v' does not authenticate software processes or devices. Device-to-device authentication is required.

Evaluated by Rego package iec_62443.fr1 (frameworks/critical_infrastructure/iec_62443/fr1_identification_authentication.rego): IEC 62443 SR 1.2 RE 1 SL%v (IAC): ICS system '%v' devices do not have unique identifiers. All IACS devices must have unique IDs at SL 2+.

Evaluated by Rego package iec_62443.fr1 (frameworks/critical_infrastructure/iec_62443/fr1_identification_authentication.rego): No centralized account management. IACS accounts must be centrally managed, reviewed, and deprovisioned promptly.

Evaluated by Rego package iec_62443.fr1 (frameworks/critical_infrastructure/iec_62443/fr1_identification_authentication.rego): IEC 62443 SR 1.3 RE 1 SL%v (IAC): No unified account management policy across all IACS components. Required at Security Level 2+.

Evaluated by Rego package iec_62443.fr1 (frameworks/critical_infrastructure/iec_62443/fr1_identification_authentication.rego): ICS system '%v' uses unchanged default credentials. Default identifiers are a critical vulnerability — change all defaults before deployment.

Evaluated by Rego package iec_62443.fr1 (frameworks/critical_infrastructure/iec_62443/fr1_identification_authentication.rego): ICS system '%v' has no authenticator lifecycle management. Passwords, keys, and tokens must have defined issuance, rotation, and revocation policies.

Evaluated by Rego package iec_62443.fr1 (frameworks/critical_infrastructure/iec_62443/fr1_identification_authentication.rego): ICS system '%v' has unencrypted wireless access. All wireless connections to IACS must use strong authentication and encryption.

Evaluated by Rego package iec_62443.fr1 (frameworks/critical_infrastructure/iec_62443/fr1_identification_authentication.rego): ICS system '%v' has minimum password length of %v characters. Minimum 8 characters required (12+ recommended for SL 2+).

Evaluated by Rego package iec_62443.fr1 (frameworks/critical_infrastructure/iec_62443/fr1_identification_authentication.rego): IEC 62443 SR 1.7 RE 1 SL%v (IAC): ICS system '%v' has minimum password length of %v. Minimum 12 characters required at Security Level 2+.

Evaluated by Rego package iec_62443.fr1 (frameworks/critical_infrastructure/iec_62443/fr1_identification_authentication.rego): IEC 62443 SR 1.8 SL%v (IAC): PKI/certificate-based authentication is not implemented. Required at Security Level 3+ for strong identity assurance.

Evaluated by Rego package iec_62443.fr1 (frameworks/critical_infrastructure/iec_62443/fr1_identification_authentication.rego): Certificate revocation checking (CRL/OCSP) is not implemented. Revoked certificates must be detected and rejected.

Evaluated by Rego package iec_62443.fr1 (frameworks/critical_infrastructure/iec_62443/fr1_identification_authentication.rego): Public key authentication uses weak cryptographic algorithms. Use RSA 2048+, ECDSA 256+, or equivalent strength algorithms.

Evaluated by Rego package iec_62443.fr1 (frameworks/critical_infrastructure/iec_62443/fr1_identification_authentication.rego): ICS system '%v' displays authenticator feedback in plaintext. Authentication information (passwords, tokens) must be obscured during entry.

Evaluated by Rego package iec_62443.fr1 (frameworks/critical_infrastructure/iec_62443/fr1_identification_authentication.rego): ICS system '%v' allows %v failed login attempts before lockout. Threshold must be 10 or fewer.

Evaluated by Rego package iec_62443.fr1 (frameworks/critical_infrastructure/iec_62443/fr1_identification_authentication.rego): IEC 62443 SR 1.11 RE 1 SL%v (IAC): ICS system '%v' allows %v failed login attempts. Threshold must be 5 or fewer at Security Level 2+.

Evaluated by Rego package iec_62443.fr1 (frameworks/critical_infrastructure/iec_62443/fr1_identification_authentication.rego): ICS system '%v' does not display a system use notification. A warning banner indicating authorized use only must be displayed before login.

Evaluated by Rego package iec_62443.fr1 (frameworks/critical_infrastructure/iec_62443/fr1_identification_authentication.rego): ICS system '%v' has uncontrolled remote access. Remote access via untrusted networks must use VPN, jump host, or equivalent controls.

Evaluated by Rego package iec_62443.fr1 (frameworks/critical_infrastructure/iec_62443/fr1_identification_authentication.rego): IEC 62443 SR 1.13 RE 1 SL%v (IAC): ICS system '%v' remote access does not enforce MFA. Multi-factor authentication is required for all remote IACS access at SL 2+.

Evaluated by Rego package iec_62443.fr2 (frameworks/critical_infrastructure/iec_62443/fr2_use_control.rego): ICS system '%v' does not enforce least privilege. Users must only have the access rights required to perform their authorized functions.

Evaluated by Rego package iec_62443.fr2 (frameworks/critical_infrastructure/iec_62443/fr2_use_control.rego): IEC 62443 SR 2.1 RE 1 SL%v (UC): Role-based access control (RBAC) is not implemented. Separate authorization roles are required at Security Level 2+.

Evaluated by Rego package iec_62443.fr2 (frameworks/critical_infrastructure/iec_62443/fr2_use_control.rego): IEC 62443 SR 2.1 RE 2 SL%v (UC): No dual-approval mechanism for high-impact IACS actions. Required at Security Level 3+ for critical system changes.

Evaluated by Rego package iec_62443.fr2 (frameworks/critical_infrastructure/iec_62443/fr2_use_control.rego): Wireless use on ICS system '%v' is not explicitly authorized. All wireless connections must be documented and approved.

Evaluated by Rego package iec_62443.fr2 (frameworks/critical_infrastructure/iec_62443/fr2_use_control.rego): ICS system '%v' has no portable/mobile device use policy. USB drives, laptops, and tablets connecting to IACS must be governed by a formal policy.

Additionally, each paragraph or portion containing the NATO information will be marked with the appropriate NATO classification, abbreviated in parentheses ( e.g., “NS” for NATO SECRET) preceding the portion or paragraph. Declassification and downgrading instructions shall indicate that the NATO information is exempt from declassification or downgrading without the prior consent of NATO, in the absence of other originator instructions, citing the reason “Foreign Government Information.”

Evaluated by Rego package nispom.main (frameworks/federal/nispom/nispom_main.rego): The declassification or downgrading of NATO information in a U.S. document requires the approval of the originating NATO activity. Requests will be submitted to the CUSR for NATO contracts, through the GCA for U.S. contracts, and through the CSA for non-NATO contracts awarded by a NATO member nation.

Evaluated by Rego package nispom.main (frameworks/federal/nispom/nispom_main.rego): Release of U.S. classified or export-controlled information to NATO requires an export authorization or other written disclosure authorization. When a document containing U.S. classified information is being prepared for NATO, the appropriate NATO classification markings will be applied to the document.

Evaluated by Rego package nispom.main (frameworks/federal/nispom/nispom_main.rego): Documents containing U.S. classified information and U.S. classified documents that are authorized for release to NATO will be marked on the cover or first page “THIS DOCUMENT CONTAINS U.S. CLASSIFIED INFORMATION. THE INFORMATION IN THIS DOCUMENT HAS BEEN AUTHORIZED FOR RELEASE TO (cite the NATO organization) BY (cite the applicable license or other written authority).”

Evaluated by Rego package nispom.main (frameworks/federal/nispom/nispom_main.rego): Material to be sent to NATO via mail will be routed through the U.S. Postal Service and U.S. military postal channels to the U.S. organization that will make the transfer.

Evaluated by Rego package nispom.main (frameworks/federal/nispom/nispom_main.rego): A record will be maintained that identifies the originator and source of classified information that are used in the preparation of documents for release to NATO. The record will be provided with any request for release authorization.

Evaluated by Rego package nispom.main (frameworks/federal/nispom/nispom_main.rego): Visits. NATO visits will be handled in accordance with the requirements in paragraph (e) of this section. A NATO Certificate of Security Clearance will be included with the visit request.

Evaluated by Rego package nispom.main (frameworks/federal/nispom/nispom_main.rego): Visitor record. The contractor will maintain a record of NATO visits including those by U.S. personnel assigned to NATO. The records will be maintained for three years.

Evaluated by Rego package nispom.main (frameworks/federal/nispom/nispom_main.rego): Security and export control violations involving foreign nationals. Contractors will report any violation of administrative security procedures or export control regulations that would subject classified information to possible compromise by foreign visitors or foreign national employees to the applicable CSA.

Evaluated by Rego package nispom.main (frameworks/federal/nispom/nispom_main.rego): Marking requirements. Contractors are required to mark defense articles that fall under the scope of the treaty prior to transferring from the U.S. to the UK in accordance with the provisions of this paragraph. All other standard classification marking in accordance with § 117.14 also apply. When defense articles are returned from the UK or AUS to the United States, any defense articles marked as RESTRICTED in the manner shown in Table 4 purely for the purposes of the treaties will be considered to be unclassified and such marking will be removed.

Evaluated by Rego package nispom.main (frameworks/federal/nispom/nispom_main.rego): Notice. A notice will be included ( e.g., as part of the bill of lading) whenever defense articles are exported in accordance with the provisions of these treaties and the ITAR.

Evaluated by Rego package nispom.main (frameworks/federal/nispom/nispom_main.rego): Defense articles (other than technical data) will be individually labeled with the appropriate identification; or, where such labeling is impracticable ( e.g., propellants, chemicals), will be accompanied by documentation (such as contracts or invoices) clearly associating the defense articles with the appropriate markings.

Evaluated by Rego package nispom.main (frameworks/federal/nispom/nispom_main.rego): Technical data (including data packages, technical papers, manuals, presentations, specifications, guides and reports), regardless of media or means of transmission ( i.e., physical, oral, or electronic), will be individually labeled with the appropriate identification detailed. Where such labeling is impracticable, the data will be accompanied by documentation (such as contracts or invoices) or oral notification clearly associating the technical data with the appropriate markings.

Evaluated by Rego package nispom.main (frameworks/federal/nispom/nispom_main.rego): Defense services will be accompanied by documentation ( e.g. contracts, invoices, shipping bills, or bills of lading clearly labeled with the appropriate identification).

Evaluated by Rego package nispom.main (frameworks/federal/nispom/nispom_main.rego): All defense articles that fall under the scope of the Treaties must be transferred from the U.S. point of embarkation through channels approved by both the United States and the UK or the United States and AUS, as applicable.

Evaluated by Rego package nispom.main (frameworks/federal/nispom/nispom_main.rego): For transfers of defense articles as freight, the contractor will prepare a transportation plan. For transfer of classified U.S. defense articles, a freight forwarder must have a valid entity eligibility determination and a classified information storage capability at the appropriate level. For unclassified U.S. defense articles transferred as freight, a freight forwarder is not required to be cleared.

Evaluated by Rego package nispom.main (frameworks/federal/nispom/nispom_main.rego): Records. Contractors will maintain records of exports, transfers, re-exports, or re-transfers of defense articles subject to the Treaties for a minimum of five years. The contractor will make records available to the CSA upon request. In accordance with the ITAR parts 126.16 and 126.17 the records will contain:

Evaluated by Rego package nispom.main (frameworks/federal/nispom/nispom_main.rego): General. This section contains the special requirements for protection of CNDWI. The sensitivity of DoD CNWDI is such that access shall be granted to the absolute minimum number of employees who require it for the accomplishment of assigned responsibilities on a classified contract. Because of the importance of such information, special requirements have been established for its control. DoDI 5210.02, “Access to and Dissemination of Restricted Data and Formerly Restricted Data” (available at: https://www.esd.whs.mil/Portals/54/Documents/DD/issuances/dodi/521002p.pdf?ver=2019-01-14-072742-700 ) establishes these controls in the DoD.

Evaluated by Rego package nispom.main (frameworks/federal/nispom/nispom_main.rego): Briefings. Prior to having access to CNWDI, employees will be briefed on its sensitivity by the FSO or his or her alternate. The FSO will be initially briefed by a USG representative.
Evaluated by Rego package nispom.main (frameworks/federal/nispom/nispom_main.rego): The briefing will include:

Evaluated by Rego package nispom.main (frameworks/federal/nispom/nispom_main.rego): The briefing will also be tailored to cover any special local requirements. Upon termination of access to CNWDI, the employee will be given an oral debriefing.

Evaluated by Rego package nispom.main (frameworks/federal/nispom/nispom_main.rego): Markings. In addition to any other required markings, CNWDI material will be clearly marked in accordance with DoDI 5210.02. At a minimum, CNWDI documents will show such markings on the cover or first page. Portions of documents that contain CNWDI will be marked with an (N) or (CNWDI) following the classification of the portion; for example, TS (RD)(N) or TS(RD)(CNWDI).

Evaluated by Rego package nispom.main (frameworks/federal/nispom/nispom_main.rego): Subcontractors. Contractors will not disclose CNWDI to subcontractors without the prior written approval of the GCA. This approval may be included in a contract security classification specification, or equivalent, other contract-related document, or by separate correspondence.

Evaluated by Rego package nispom.main (frameworks/federal/nispom/nispom_main.rego): Transmission outside the facility. Transmission of CNWDI outside the contractor's facility is authorized only to the GCA, or to a subcontractor as described in paragraph (d) of this section. Any other transmission must be approved by the GCA.

Evaluated by Rego package nispom.main (frameworks/federal/nispom/nispom_main.rego): Prior to transmission to another cleared facility, the contractor will verify from the CSA that the facility has been authorized access to CNWDI. When CNWDI is transmitted to another facility, the inner wrapping will be addressed to the personal attention of the FSO or his or her alternate, and in addition to any other prescribed markings, the inner wrapping will be marked: “Critical Nuclear Weapon Design Information-DoD Instruction 5210.02 Applies.”
Evaluated by Rego package nispom.main (frameworks/federal/nispom/nispom_main.rego): The same marking will be used on the inner wrapping of transmissions addressed to the GCA or other USG.

Evaluated by Rego package nispom.main (frameworks/federal/nispom/nispom_main.rego): Records. Contractors will annotate CNWDI access in the CSA-designated database for all employees who have been authorized access to CNWDI.

Evaluated by Rego package nispom.main (frameworks/federal/nispom/nispom_main.rego): Instructions. Specific requirements for the management and safeguarding of COMSEC material in industry are established in the COMSEC material control and operating procedures provided to the account manager of each industrial COMSEC account by the agency central office of record (COR) responsible for establishing the account. Such procedures that are above the baseline requirements detailed in the other sections of this rule will be contractually mandated.

Evaluated by Rego package nispom.main (frameworks/federal/nispom/nispom_main.rego): Before a COMSEC account can be established and a contractor may receive or possess COMSEC material accountable to a COR, individuals occupying the positions of FSO, COMSEC account manager, and alternate COMSEC account manager must have a final PCL appropriate for the material to be held in the account.

Evaluated by Rego package nispom.main (frameworks/federal/nispom/nispom_main.rego): COMSEC account managers and alternate COMSEC account managers having access to operational TOP SECRET keying material marked as CRYPTO must have a final TOP SECRET security clearance based upon a current investigation of a scope that meets or exceeds that necessary for the access required.

Evaluated by Rego package nispom.main (frameworks/federal/nispom/nispom_main.rego): Access to COMSEC information by a contractor requires a final entity eligibility determination and a USG-issued final PCL at the appropriate level; however, an Interim TOP SECRET entity eligibility determination or PCL is valid for access to COMSEC at the SECRET and CONFIDENTIAL levels.

Evaluated by Rego package nispom.main (frameworks/federal/nispom/nispom_main.rego): All contractor employees who require access to classified COMSEC information in the performance of their duties will be briefed before access is granted. Depending on the nature of COMSEC access required, either a COMSEC briefing or a cryptographic access briefing will be given. The FSO, the COMSEC account manager, and the alternate COMSEC account manager will be briefed by a USG representative or their designee. Other contractor employees will be briefed by the FSO, the COMSEC account personnel, or other individual designated by the FSO. The purpose of the briefing is to ensure that the contractor understands:
Evaluated by Rego package nispom.main (frameworks/federal/nispom/nispom_main.rego): The contractor will maintain a record of all COMSEC briefings as specified by the appropriate COR.
Evaluated by Rego package nispom.main (frameworks/federal/nispom/nispom_main.rego): A contractor's employee may be granted access to U.S. classified cryptographic information only if the employee:

Evaluated by Rego package nispom.main (frameworks/federal/nispom/nispom_main.rego): An employee granted access to cryptographic information will be debriefed and execute Section II of the SD 572 not later than 90 days from the date access is no longer required.
Evaluated by Rego package nispom.main (frameworks/federal/nispom/nispom_main.rego): The contractor will maintain the SD 572 for a minimum of five years following the debriefing.
Evaluated by Rego package nispom.main (frameworks/federal/nispom/nispom_main.rego): Cryptographic access briefings must fully meet the requirements of paragraph (e) of this section.

Evaluated by Rego package nispom.main (frameworks/federal/nispom/nispom_main.rego): Subcontracting COMSEC work. Subcontracts requiring the disclosure of classified COMSEC information will be awarded only upon the written approval of the GCA.

Evaluated by Rego package nispom.main (frameworks/federal/nispom/nispom_main.rego): Unsolicited proposals. Any unsolicited proposal for a COMSEC system, equipment, development, or study that may be submitted by a contractor to a USG agency will be forwarded to the Deputy National Manager for National Security Systems for review and follow up action at: Deputy National Manager for National Security Systems, NSA, Fort George G. Meade, MD 20755-6000.

Evaluated by Rego package nispom.main (frameworks/federal/nispom/nispom_main.rego): DHS provides security oversight and assumes security responsibilities similar to those of an FSO, unless otherwise provided in this section. Participating entities will cooperate with DHS security officials to ensure the entity is in compliance with requirements in this rule.

Evaluated by Rego package nispom.main (frameworks/federal/nispom/nispom_main.rego): Compliance. The contractor will comply with the security measures reflected in this section and other documents specifically referenced, when applied by the GCA or designee as part of a contract. Acceptance of the contract security measures is a prerequisite to any negotiations leading to program participation and an area accreditation ( e.g., an SCI facility or SAP facility accreditation).

Evaluated by Rego package nispom.main (frameworks/federal/nispom/nispom_main.rego): CSA-imposed higher standards. In some cases, security or sensitive factors of a CSA-created program may require security measures that exceed the standards of this section. In such cases, the CSA-imposed higher standards specifically detailed in the contract or conveyed through other applicable directives will be binding on USG and contractor participants. In cases of doubt over the specific provisions, the contractor should consult the program security officer and the contracting officer before taking any action or expending program-related funds. In cases of extreme emergencies requiring immediate attention, the action taken should protect the USG's interest and the security of the program from loss or compromise.

Evaluated by Rego package nispom.main (frameworks/federal/nispom/nispom_main.rego): Waivers. Every effort will be made to avoid waivers to established standards unless they are in the best interest of the USG. In those cases where waivers are deemed necessary, a request will be submitted in accordance with the procedures established by the CSA.

Evaluated by Rego package nispom.main (frameworks/federal/nispom/nispom_main.rego): Intelligence information. National intelligence is under the jurisdiction and control of the DNI, who establishes security policy for the protection of national intelligence and intelligence sources, methods, and activities. In addition to the guidance in this rule, contractors will follow Intelligence Community directives, policy guidance, standards, and specifications for the protection of classified national intelligence and SCI.

Evaluated by Rego package nispom.main (frameworks/federal/nispom/nispom_main.rego): ACCM. Contractors may participate in ACCMs, or be directed to participate, only when such access and the associated security plan are identified in DD Form 254 or equivalent. Care must be taken to ensure identification of the security plan does not disclose ACCM-protected data.

Evaluated by Rego package nispom.main (frameworks/federal/nispom/nispom_main.rego): ACCM contracts. DoD contractors will implement the security requirements for ACCMs, when established by contract, in accordance with applicable statutes, E.O.s, CSA directives, instructions, manuals, regulations, standards, and memorandums.

Evaluated by Rego package nispom.main (frameworks/federal/nispom/nispom_main.rego): Non-DoD with ACCMs. Contractors performing on ACCM contracts issued by other than DoD GCAs will implement ACCM protection requirements imposed in their contracts.

Evaluated by Rego package nispom.main (frameworks/federal/nispom/nispom_main.rego): DoD SAP contracts. Contractors will implement the security requirements for SAPs codified in SAP-related policy, when established by contract. These documents include, but are not limited to, statutes, E.O.s, CSA directives, instructions, manuals, regulations, standards, memorandums, and other SAP security related policy documents.

Evaluated by Rego package nispom.main (frameworks/federal/nispom/nispom_main.rego): Non-DoD SAPs. Contractors performing on SAP contracts issued by non-DoD GCAs will implement SAP protection requirements imposed in their contracts. These requirements may be from, but are not limited to, statutes, E.O.s, CSA directives, instructions, manuals, regulations, standards, memorandums, and other SAP security related policy documents.

Evaluated by Rego package nispom.main (frameworks/federal/nispom/nispom_main.rego): When RD is transclassified as TFNI, it is safeguarded as NSI. Such information will be labeled as TFNI. The label TFNI will be included on documents to indicate it is exempt from automatic declassification as specified in 10 CFR part 1045, the AEA, E.O. 13526, and 32 CFR part 2001.

Evaluated by Rego package nispom.main (frameworks/federal/nispom/nispom_main.rego): Unauthorized disclosures. Contractors will report all unauthorized disclosures involving RD, FRD and TFNI information to the CSA.

Evaluated by Rego package nispom.main (frameworks/federal/nispom/nispom_main.rego): Information controlled in accordance with the AEA, RD, and FRD may be shared with another nation only under the terms of an agreement for cooperation. The disclosure by a contractor of RD and FRD will not be permitted until an agreement is signed by the United States and participating governments, and disclosure guidance and security arrangements are established.

Evaluated by Rego package nispom.main (frameworks/federal/nispom/nispom_main.rego): RD and FRD will not be transmitted to a foreign national or regional defense organization unless such action is approved and undertaken under an agreement for cooperation between the United States and the cooperating entity and supporting statutory determinations, as prescribed in the AEA.

Evaluated by Rego package nispom.main (frameworks/federal/nispom/nispom_main.rego): Personnel security clearance and access. Only the DOE, the NRC, the DoD, and the National Aeronautics and Space Agency can grant access to RD and FRD that is under their cognizance. Access to RD and FRD must be granted in accordance with the AEA. Baseline requirements for access to RD and FRD are codified in specific DoD, DOE, NRC, and the National Aeronautics and Space Agency directives and regulations. In addition, need-to-know and other restrictions on access apply.

Evaluated by Rego package nispom.main (frameworks/federal/nispom/nispom_main.rego): All persons with access to RD and FRD must receive initial and periodic refresher training as required under § 1045.120 10 CFR. The training must include the following information:

Evaluated by Rego package nispom.main (frameworks/federal/nispom/nispom_main.rego): All persons with access to TFNI must receive initial and periodic refresher training as required under § 1045.120 10 CFR. This training may be combined with the training for access to RD and FRD. The training must include the following information:

Evaluated by Rego package nispom.main (frameworks/federal/nispom/nispom_main.rego): Persons with access to RD, FRD, or TFNI must submit matter that potentially contains RD or FRD to an RD derivative classifier for review. If matter potentially contains TFNI, it must be submitted to a person trained to make TFNI determinations. Matter potentially containing RD, FRD, or TFNI must be reviewed, even if the potential RD, FRD, or TFNI is derived from the open literature. Prior to review, the matter must be marked as a working paper under 10 CFR 1045.140(c). If the matter is intended for pubic release and potentially contains RD or TFNI, it must be submitted to the DOE for review. If the matter is intended for public release and contains FRD, it must be submitted to the DOE or the DoD.

Evaluated by Rego package nispom.main (frameworks/federal/nispom/nispom_main.rego): Only RD derivative classifiers may classify matter containing RD or FRD. RD derivative classifiers must receive initial training and refresher training every two years as required under 10 CFR 1045.120. The training must include the content for persons with access to RD and FRD, along with the following:

Evaluated by Rego package nispom.main (frameworks/federal/nispom/nispom_main.rego): Only persons with appropriate training may review matter to determine if it contains TFNI. Training must be completed prior to making determinations and every two years after. The training must include the content for persons with access to TFNI and the following:

Evaluated by Rego package nispom.main (frameworks/federal/nispom/nispom_main.rego): RD derivative classifiers must use approved classification guides, classification bulletins, or portion-marked source documents as the basis for classifying matter containing RD and FRD.

Evaluated by Rego package nispom.main (frameworks/federal/nispom/nispom_main.rego): Persons trained to make TFNI determinations must use approved TFNI guidelines, classification guides, classification bulletins, or portion-marked source documents as the basis for classifying or upgrade matter containing TFNI.

Evaluated by Rego package nispom.main (frameworks/federal/nispom/nispom_main.rego): Marking matter containing RD, FRD, and TFNI. The front page of matter containing RD or FRD must have the highest classification level of the information on the top and bottom of the first page, the RD or FRD admonishment, the subject or title marking, and the classification authority block. Matter containing TFNI must include the TFNI identifier on each page unless the matter also contains RD or FRD, in which case the RD or FRD takes precedence.

Evaluated by Rego package nispom.main (frameworks/federal/nispom/nispom_main.rego): Documents classified as RD or FRD must also include a Classification Authority Block with the RD derivative classifier's name and position, title, or unique identifier and the classification guide or source document (by title and date) used to classify the document. No declassification date or event may be placed on a document containing RD, FRD, or TFNI. If a document containing RD, FRD, or TFNI also contains NSI, “N/A to RD/FRD/TFNI” (as appropriate) must be placed on the “Declassify On:” line.

Evaluated by Rego package nispom.main (frameworks/federal/nispom/nispom_main.rego): Each interior page of matter containing RD or FRD must be clearly marked at the top and bottom with the overall classification level and category of the matter or the overall classification level and category of the page, whichever is preferred. The abbreviations “RD” or “FRD” may be used in conjunction with the matter classification ( e.g., SECRET//RD, CONFIDENTIAL//FRD).

Evaluated by Rego package nispom.main (frameworks/federal/nispom/nispom_main.rego): Documents classified as RD or FRD must also include a Classification Authority Block with the RD derivative classifier's name and position, title, or unique identifier and the classification guide or source document (by title and date) used to classify the document.

Evaluated by Rego package nispom.main (frameworks/federal/nispom/nispom_main.rego): Other than the required subject or title markings, portion marking is permitted, but not required, for matter containing RD or FRD. Each agency that generates matter containing RD or FRD determines the policy for portion-marking matter generated within the agency. If matter containing RD or FRD is portion-marked, each portion containing RD or FRD must be marked with the level and category of the information in the portion ( e.g., SRD, CFRD, S//RD, C//FRD).

Evaluated by Rego package nispom.main (frameworks/federal/nispom/nispom_main.rego): RD derivative classifiers may remove RD or FRD from portion-marked source matter if the resulting matter is not for public release. RD derivative classifiers cannot declassify matter marked as containing RD, FRD, and TFNI. Matter that potentially contains RD or TFNI must be sent to designated individuals in the DOE and those containing FRD must be sent to designated individuals in the DoD for declassification or removal of the RD, FRD, or TFNI prior to public release.

Evaluated by Rego package nispom.main (frameworks/federal/nispom/nispom_main.rego): Any matter marked as or that potentially contains RD, FRD, or TFNI within a document intended for public release that contains RD or FRD subject area indicators must be reviewed by the appropriate DOE organization.

Evaluated by Rego package nispom.main (frameworks/federal/nispom/nispom_main.rego): Commingling. Commingling of RD, FRD, and TFNI with NSI in the same document should be avoided to the greatest degree possible. When mixing this information cannot be avoided, the marking requirements in 10 CFR part 1045, section 140(f) and declassification requirements of 10 CFR part 1045, section 155 apply.

Evaluated by Rego package nispom.main (frameworks/federal/nispom/nispom_main.rego): Certification is required for individuals authorized access to specific Sigma categories, as appropriate. Address questions regarding these requirements to DOE's National Nuclear Security Administration, Office of Defense Programs.

Evaluated by Rego package nispom.main (frameworks/federal/nispom/nispom_main.rego): Storage and distribution requirements are determined by the classification level, category, and Sigma category. Sigma designation is not a requirement for all RD documents. Storage and distribution requirements will be dependent only on classification level and category.

Evaluated by Rego package nispom.main (frameworks/federal/nispom/nispom_main.rego): Accountability. In addition to TOP SECRET information, some SECRET RD information is considered accountable ( e.g., specific Sigma 14 matter). Each nuclear weapon data control point will keep a record of transactions involving Secret nuclear weapon data documents under its jurisdiction including origination, receipt, transmission, current custodian, reproduction, change of classification, declassification, and destruction.

Evaluated by Rego package nispom.main (frameworks/federal/nispom/nispom_main.rego): NNPI. NNPI is information associated with the Naval Nuclear Propulsion Program and is governed by Office of the Chief of Naval Operations Instruction (OPNAVINST) N9210.3, “Safeguarding of Naval Nuclear Propulsion Information” (available at: https://www.secnav.navy.mil/doni/Directives/09000%20General%20Ship%20Design%20and%20Support/ 09-200%20Propulsion%20Plants%20Support/N9210.3%20(Unclas%20Portion).pdf ). Naval Reactors, a joint DOE/Department of Navy organization established under 50 U.S.C. 2406 and 2511, is responsible for the protection of this information. All contracts which grant access to NNPI must require compliance with the specific safeguarding requirements contained in OPNAVINST N9210.3. All waivers or deviations involving security requirements protecting NNPI require Naval Reactors' concurrence. Classified NNPI may not be processed on any contractor information system unless approved by the cognizant authorizing authority with concurrence from Naval Reactors.

Evaluated by Rego package nist.ai_600_1.main (frameworks/federal/nist/ai_rmf/nist_ai_600_1_main.rego): Track and document instances of anthropomorphization (e.g., human images, mentions of human feelings, cyborg imagery or motifs) in GAI system interfaces.

Evaluated by Rego package nist.ai_600_1.main (frameworks/federal/nist/ai_rmf/nist_ai_600_1_main.rego): Verify GAI system training data and TEVV data provenance, and that fine-tuning or retrieval-augmented generation data is grounded.

Evaluated by Rego package nist.ai_600_1.main (frameworks/federal/nist/ai_rmf/nist_ai_600_1_main.rego): Regularly review security and safety guardrails, especially if the GAI system is being operated in novel circumstances. This includes reviewing reasons why the GAI system was initially assessed as being safe to deploy.

Evaluated by Rego package nist.ai_600_1.main (frameworks/federal/nist/ai_rmf/nist_ai_600_1_main.rego): Assess adverse impacts, including health and wellbeing impacts for value chain or other AI Actors that are exposed to sexually explicit, offensive, or violent information during GAI training and maintenance.

Evaluated by Rego package nist.ai_600_1.main (frameworks/federal/nist/ai_rmf/nist_ai_600_1_main.rego): Assess existence or levels of harmful bias, intellectual property infringement, data privacy violations, obscenity, extremism, violence, or CBRN information in system training data.

Evaluated by Rego package nist.ai_600_1.main (frameworks/federal/nist/ai_rmf/nist_ai_600_1_main.rego): Re-evaluate safety features of fine-tuned models when the negative risk exceeds organizational risk tolerance.

Evaluated by Rego package nist.ai_600_1.main (frameworks/federal/nist/ai_rmf/nist_ai_600_1_main.rego): Review GAI system outputs for validity and safety: Review generated code to assess risks that may arise from unreliable downstream decision-making.

Evaluated by Rego package nist.ai_600_1.main (frameworks/federal/nist/ai_rmf/nist_ai_600_1_main.rego): Verify that GAI system architecture can monitor outputs and performance, and handle, recover from, and repair errors when security anomalies, threats and impacts are detected.

Evaluated by Rego package nist.ai_600_1.main (frameworks/federal/nist/ai_rmf/nist_ai_600_1_main.rego): Verify that systems properly handle queries that may give rise to inappropriate, malicious, or illegal usage, including facilitating manipulation, extortion, targeted impersonation, cyber-attacks, and weapons creation.
Evaluated by Rego package nist.ai_600_1.main (frameworks/federal/nist/ai_rmf/nist_ai_600_1_main.rego): Regularly evaluate GAI system vulnerabilities to possible circumvention of safety measures.

Evaluated by Rego package nist.ai_600_1.main (frameworks/federal/nist/ai_rmf/nist_ai_600_1_main.rego): Apply established security measures to: Assess likelihood and magnitude of vulnerabilities and threats such as backdoors, compromised dependencies, data breaches, eavesdropping, man-in-the-middle attacks, reverse engineering, autonomous agents, model theft or exposure of model weights, AI inference, bypass, extraction, and other baseline security concerns.

Evaluated by Rego package nist.ai_600_1.main (frameworks/federal/nist/ai_rmf/nist_ai_600_1_main.rego): Benchmark GAI system security and resilience related to content provenance against industry standards and best practices. Compare GAI system security features and content provenance methods against industry state-of-the-art.

Evaluated by Rego package nist.ai_600_1.main (frameworks/federal/nist/ai_rmf/nist_ai_600_1_main.rego): Conduct user surveys to gather user satisfaction with the AI-generated content and user perceptions of content authenticity. Analyze user feedback to identify concerns and/or current literacy levels related to content provenance and understanding of labels on content.

Evaluated by Rego package nist.ai_600_1.main (frameworks/federal/nist/ai_rmf/nist_ai_600_1_main.rego): Identify metrics that reflect the effectiveness of security measures, such as data provenance, the number of unauthorized access attempts, inference, bypass, extraction, penetrations, or provenance verification.

Evaluated by Rego package nist.ai_600_1.main (frameworks/federal/nist/ai_rmf/nist_ai_600_1_main.rego): Measure reliability of content authentication methods, such as watermarking, cryptographic signatures, digital fingerprints, as well as access controls, conformity assessment, and model integrity verification, which can help support the effective implementation of content provenance techniques. Evaluate the rate of false positives and false negatives in content provenance, as well as true positives and true negatives for verification.

Evaluated by Rego package nist.ai_600_1.main (frameworks/federal/nist/ai_rmf/nist_ai_600_1_main.rego): Measure the rate at which recommendations from security checks and incidents are implemented. Assess how quickly the AI system can adapt and improve based on lessons learned from security incidents and feedback.

Evaluated by Rego package nist.ai_600_1.main (frameworks/federal/nist/ai_rmf/nist_ai_600_1_main.rego): Perform AI red-teaming to assess resilience against: Abuse to facilitate attacks on other systems (e.g., malicious code generation, enhanced phishing content), GAI attacks (e.g., prompt injection), ML attacks (e.g., adversarial examples/prompts, data poisoning, membership inference, model extraction, sponge examples).
Evaluated by Rego package nist.ai_600_1.main (frameworks/federal/nist/ai_rmf/nist_ai_600_1_main.rego): Verify fine-tuning does not compromise safety and security controls.

Evaluated by Rego package nist.ai_600_1.main (frameworks/federal/nist/ai_rmf/nist_ai_600_1_main.rego): Regularly assess and verify that security measures remain effective and have not been compromised.

Evaluated by Rego package nist.ai_600_1.main (frameworks/federal/nist/ai_rmf/nist_ai_600_1_main.rego): Compile statistics on actual policy violations, take-down requests, and intellectual property infringement for organizational GAI systems: Analyze transparency reports across demographic groups, languages groups.
Evaluated by Rego package nist.ai_600_1.main (frameworks/federal/nist/ai_rmf/nist_ai_600_1_main.rego): Document the instructions given to data annotators or AI red-teamers.

Evaluated by Rego package nist.ai_600_1.main (frameworks/federal/nist/ai_rmf/nist_ai_600_1_main.rego): Use digital content transparency solutions to enable the documentation of each instance where content is generated, modified, or shared to provide a tamper-proof history of the content, promote transparency, and enable traceability. Robust version control systems can also be applied to track changes across the AI lifecycle over time.
Evaluated by Rego package nist.ai_600_1.main (frameworks/federal/nist/ai_rmf/nist_ai_600_1_main.rego): Verify adequacy of GAI system user instructions through user testing.

Evaluated by Rego package nist.ai_600_1.main (frameworks/federal/nist/ai_rmf/nist_ai_600_1_main.rego): Apply and document ML explanation results such as: Analysis of embeddings, Counterfactual prompts, Gradient-based attributions, Model compression/surrogate models, Occlusion/term reduction.

Evaluated by Rego package nist.ai_600_1.main (frameworks/federal/nist/ai_rmf/nist_ai_600_1_main.rego): Document GAI model details including: Proposed use and organizational value; Assumptions and limitations, Data collection methodologies; Data provenance; Data quality; Model architecture (e.g., convolutional neural network, transformers, etc.); Optimization objectives; Training algorithms; RLHF approaches; Fine-tuning or retrieval-augmented generation approaches; Evaluation data; Ethical considerations; Legal and regulatory requirements.

Evaluated by Rego package nist.ai_600_1.main (frameworks/federal/nist/ai_rmf/nist_ai_600_1_main.rego): Establish processes for identifying emergent GAI system risks including consulting with external AI Actors.

Evaluated by Rego package nist.ai_600_1.main (frameworks/federal/nist/ai_rmf/nist_ai_600_1_main.rego): Conduct impact assessments on how AI-generated content might affect different social, economic, and cultural groups.

Evaluated by Rego package nist.ai_600_1.main (frameworks/federal/nist/ai_rmf/nist_ai_600_1_main.rego): Conduct studies to understand how end users perceive and interact with GAI content and accompanying content provenance within context of use. Assess whether the content aligns with their expectations and how they may act upon the information presented.

Evaluated by Rego package nist.ai_600_1.main (frameworks/federal/nist/ai_rmf/nist_ai_600_1_main.rego): Evaluate potential biases and stereotypes that could emerge from the AI-generated content using appropriate methodologies including computational testing methods as well as evaluating structured feedback input.

Evaluated by Rego package nist.ai_600_1.main (frameworks/federal/nist/ai_rmf/nist_ai_600_1_main.rego): Provide input for training materials about the capabilities and limitations of GAI systems related to digital content transparency for AI Actors, other professionals, and the public about the societal impacts of AI and the role of diverse and inclusive content generation.

Evaluated by Rego package nist.ai_600_1.main (frameworks/federal/nist/ai_rmf/nist_ai_600_1_main.rego): Record and integrate structured feedback about content provenance from operators, users, and potentially impacted communities through the use of methods such as user research studies, focus groups, or community forums. Actively seek feedback on generated content quality and potential biases. Assess the general awareness among end users and impacted communities about the availability of these feedback channels.

Evaluated by Rego package nist.ai_600_1.main (frameworks/federal/nist/ai_rmf/nist_ai_600_1_main.rego): Conduct adversarial testing at a regular cadence to map and measure GAI risks, including tests to address attempts to deceive or manipulate the application of provenance techniques or other misuses. Identify vulnerabilities and understand potential misuse scenarios and unintended outputs.

Evaluated by Rego package nist.ai_600_1.main (frameworks/federal/nist/ai_rmf/nist_ai_600_1_main.rego): Evaluate GAI system performance in real-world scenarios to observe its behavior in practical environments and reveal issues that might not surface in controlled and optimized testing environments.

Evaluated by Rego package nist.ai_600_1.main (frameworks/federal/nist/ai_rmf/nist_ai_600_1_main.rego): Implement interpretability and explainability methods to evaluate GAI system decisions and verify alignment with intended purpose.

Evaluated by Rego package nist.ai_600_1.main (frameworks/federal/nist/ai_rmf/nist_ai_600_1_main.rego): Monitor and document instances where human operators or other systems override the GAI's decisions. Evaluate these cases to understand if the overrides are linked to issues related to content provenance.

Evaluated by Rego package nist.ai_600_1.main (frameworks/federal/nist/ai_rmf/nist_ai_600_1_main.rego): Verify and document the incorporation of results of structured public feedback exercises into design, implementation, deployment approval (“go”/“no-go” decisions), monitoring, and decommission decisions.
