control-implementations.description: Controls of nist_ai_rmf evaluated by the Rego Policy Libraries (92 controls, 2 Rego modules).

implemented-requirements.description: Evaluated by Rego package nist.ai_rmf (frameworks/federal/nist/ai_rmf/nist_ai_rmf.rego): AI governance roles and responsibilities are not defined. Designate accountability for AI risk management.
Evaluated by Rego package nist.ai_rmf (frameworks/federal/nist/ai_rmf/nist_ai_rmf.rego): AI risk tolerance has not been defined. Organizations must establish acceptable risk levels for AI systems.
Evaluated by Rego package nist.ai_rmf (frameworks/federal/nist/ai_rmf/nist_ai_rmf.rego): Team diversity has not been considered in AI development. Diverse teams reduce the risk of bias in AI systems.

Evaluated by Rego package nist.ai_rmf (frameworks/federal/nist/ai_rmf/nist_ai_rmf.rego): Organizational training on AI risk has not been conducted. Workforce must understand AI risks and responsibilities.
Evaluated by Rego package nist.ai_rmf (frameworks/federal/nist/ai_rmf/nist_ai_rmf.rego): AI system intended use is not documented. Document intended uses, users, and deployment context.
Evaluated by Rego package nist.ai_rmf (frameworks/federal/nist/ai_rmf/nist_ai_rmf.rego): AI risk metrics are not defined. Establish quantitative and qualitative measures for AI risks.

Evaluated by Rego package nist.ai_rmf (frameworks/federal/nist/ai_rmf/nist_ai_rmf.rego): Bias testing has not been conducted. Test for demographic biases and disparate impacts across population groups.

Evaluated by Rego package nist.ai_rmf (frameworks/federal/nist/ai_rmf/nist_ai_rmf.rego): AI performance is not monitored post-deployment. Ongoing monitoring is required to detect performance degradation and drift.
Evaluated by Rego package nist.ai_rmf (frameworks/federal/nist/ai_rmf/nist_ai_rmf.rego): Privacy risks from AI have not been assessed. Evaluate data privacy risks including inference attacks.

Evaluated by Rego package nist.ai_rmf (frameworks/federal/nist/ai_rmf/nist_ai_rmf.rego): AI explainability has not been assessed. Evaluate the degree to which AI decisions can be explained to affected parties.

Evaluated by Rego package nist.ai_rmf (frameworks/federal/nist/ai_rmf/nist_ai_rmf.rego): Regular risk reassessments are not scheduled. AI risks must be reassessed as the system and its context evolve.

Evaluated by Rego package nist.ai_rmf (frameworks/federal/nist/ai_rmf/nist_ai_rmf.rego): Risk treatment plans are not documented. Document how each identified risk will be mitigated, accepted, transferred, or avoided.
Evaluated by Rego package nist.ai_rmf (frameworks/federal/nist/ai_rmf/nist_ai_rmf.rego): No human override capability. AI systems making consequential decisions must support human override.

Evaluated by Rego package nist.ai_rmf (frameworks/federal/nist/ai_rmf/nist_ai_rmf.rego): No AI system retirement plan. Document how the system will be safely retired and what happens to its data and models.
Evaluated by Rego package nist.ai_rmf.main (frameworks/federal/nist/ai_rmf/nist_ai_rmf_main.rego): Legal and regulatory requirements involving AI are understood, managed, and documented.

Evaluated by Rego package nist.ai_rmf.main (frameworks/federal/nist/ai_rmf/nist_ai_rmf_main.rego): The characteristics of trustworthy AI are integrated into organizational policies, processes, procedures, and practices.

Evaluated by Rego package nist.ai_rmf.main (frameworks/federal/nist/ai_rmf/nist_ai_rmf_main.rego): Processes, procedures, and practices are in place to determine the needed level of risk management activities based on the organization’s risk tolerance.

Evaluated by Rego package nist.ai_rmf.main (frameworks/federal/nist/ai_rmf/nist_ai_rmf_main.rego): The risk management process and its outcomes are established through transparent policies, procedures, and other controls based on organizational risk priorities.

Evaluated by Rego package nist.ai_rmf.main (frameworks/federal/nist/ai_rmf/nist_ai_rmf_main.rego): Ongoing monitoring and periodic review of the risk management process and its outcomes are planned and organizational roles and responsibilities clearly defined, including determining the frequency of periodic review.

Evaluated by Rego package nist.ai_rmf.main (frameworks/federal/nist/ai_rmf/nist_ai_rmf_main.rego): Mechanisms are in place to inventory AI systems and are resourced according to organizational risk priorities.

Evaluated by Rego package nist.ai_rmf.main (frameworks/federal/nist/ai_rmf/nist_ai_rmf_main.rego): Processes and procedures are in place for decommissioning and phasing out AI systems safely and in a manner that does not increase risks or decrease the organization’s trustworthiness.

Evaluated by Rego package nist.ai_rmf.main (frameworks/federal/nist/ai_rmf/nist_ai_rmf_main.rego): Roles and responsibilities and lines of communication related to mapping, measuring, and managing AI risks are documented and are clear to individuals and teams throughout the organization.

Evaluated by Rego package nist.ai_rmf.main (frameworks/federal/nist/ai_rmf/nist_ai_rmf_main.rego): The organization’s personnel and partners receive AI risk management training to enable them to perform their duties and responsibilities consistent with related policies, procedures, and agreements.

Evaluated by Rego package nist.ai_rmf.main (frameworks/federal/nist/ai_rmf/nist_ai_rmf_main.rego): Executive leadership of the organization takes responsibility for decisions about risks associated with AI system development and deployment.

Evaluated by Rego package nist.ai_rmf.main (frameworks/federal/nist/ai_rmf/nist_ai_rmf_main.rego): Decision-making related to mapping, measuring, and managing AI risks throughout the lifecycle is informed by a diverse team (e.g., diversity of demographics, disciplines, experience, expertise, and backgrounds).

Evaluated by Rego package nist.ai_rmf.main (frameworks/federal/nist/ai_rmf/nist_ai_rmf_main.rego): Policies and procedures are in place to define and differentiate roles and responsibilities for human-AI configurations and oversight of AI systems.

Evaluated by Rego package nist.ai_rmf.main (frameworks/federal/nist/ai_rmf/nist_ai_rmf_main.rego): Organizational policies and practices are in place to foster a critical thinking and safety-first mindset in the design, development, deployment, and uses of AI systems to minimize potential negative impacts.

Evaluated by Rego package nist.ai_rmf.main (frameworks/federal/nist/ai_rmf/nist_ai_rmf_main.rego): Organizational teams document the risks and potential impacts of the AI technology they design, develop, deploy, evaluate, and use, and they communicate about the impacts more broadly.

Evaluated by Rego package nist.ai_rmf.main (frameworks/federal/nist/ai_rmf/nist_ai_rmf_main.rego): Organizational practices are in place to enable AI testing, identification of incidents, and information sharing.

Evaluated by Rego package nist.ai_rmf.main (frameworks/federal/nist/ai_rmf/nist_ai_rmf_main.rego): Organizational policies and practices are in place to collect, consider, prioritize, and integrate feedback from those external to the team that developed or deployed the AI system regarding the potential individual and societal impacts related to AI risks.

Evaluated by Rego package nist.ai_rmf.main (frameworks/federal/nist/ai_rmf/nist_ai_rmf_main.rego): Mechanisms are established to enable the team that developed or deployed AI systems to regularly incorporate adjudicated feedback from relevant AI actors into system design and implementation.

Evaluated by Rego package nist.ai_rmf.main (frameworks/federal/nist/ai_rmf/nist_ai_rmf_main.rego): Policies and procedures are in place that address AI risks associated with third-party entities, including risks of infringement of a third-party’s intellectual property or other rights.

Evaluated by Rego package nist.ai_rmf.main (frameworks/federal/nist/ai_rmf/nist_ai_rmf_main.rego): Contingency processes are in place to handle failures or incidents in third-party data or AI systems deemed to be high-risk.

Evaluated by Rego package nist.ai_rmf.main (frameworks/federal/nist/ai_rmf/nist_ai_rmf_main.rego): A determination is made as to whether the AI system achieves its intended purposes and stated objectives and whether its development or deployment should proceed.

Evaluated by Rego package nist.ai_rmf.main (frameworks/federal/nist/ai_rmf/nist_ai_rmf_main.rego): Treatment of documented AI risks is prioritized based on impact, likelihood, and available resources or methods.

Evaluated by Rego package nist.ai_rmf.main (frameworks/federal/nist/ai_rmf/nist_ai_rmf_main.rego): Responses to the AI risks deemed high priority, as identified by the MAP function, are developed, planned, and documented. Risk response options can include mitigating, transferring, avoiding, or accepting.

Evaluated by Rego package nist.ai_rmf.main (frameworks/federal/nist/ai_rmf/nist_ai_rmf_main.rego): Negative residual risks (defined as the sum of all unmitigated risks) to both downstream acquirers of AI systems and end users are documented.

Evaluated by Rego package nist.ai_rmf.main (frameworks/federal/nist/ai_rmf/nist_ai_rmf_main.rego): Resources required to manage AI risks are taken into account – along with viable non-AI alternative systems, approaches, or methods – to reduce the magnitude or likelihood of potential impacts.
Evaluated by Rego package nist.ai_rmf.main (frameworks/federal/nist/ai_rmf/nist_ai_rmf_main.rego): Mechanisms are in place and applied to sustain the value of deployed AI systems.

Evaluated by Rego package nist.ai_rmf.main (frameworks/federal/nist/ai_rmf/nist_ai_rmf_main.rego): Procedures are followed to respond to and recover from a previously unknown risk when it is identified.

Evaluated by Rego package nist.ai_rmf.main (frameworks/federal/nist/ai_rmf/nist_ai_rmf_main.rego): Mechanisms are in place and applied, and responsibilities are assigned and understood, to supersede, disengage, or deactivate AI systems that demonstrate performance or outcomes inconsistent with intended use.

Evaluated by Rego package nist.ai_rmf.main (frameworks/federal/nist/ai_rmf/nist_ai_rmf_main.rego): AI risks and benefits from third-party resources are regularly monitored, and risk controls are applied and documented.

Evaluated by Rego package nist.ai_rmf.main (frameworks/federal/nist/ai_rmf/nist_ai_rmf_main.rego): Pre-trained models which are used for development are monitored as part of AI system regular monitoring and maintenance.

Evaluated by Rego package nist.ai_rmf.main (frameworks/federal/nist/ai_rmf/nist_ai_rmf_main.rego): Post-deployment AI system monitoring plans are implemented, including mechanisms for capturing and evaluating input from users and other relevant AI actors, appeal and override, decommissioning, incident response, recovery, and change management.

Evaluated by Rego package nist.ai_rmf.main (frameworks/federal/nist/ai_rmf/nist_ai_rmf_main.rego): Measurable activities for continual improvements are integrated into AI system updates and include regular engagement with interested parties, including relevant AI actors.

Evaluated by Rego package nist.ai_rmf.main (frameworks/federal/nist/ai_rmf/nist_ai_rmf_main.rego): Incidents and errors are communicated to relevant AI actors, including affected communities. Processes for tracking, responding to, and recovering from incidents and errors are followed and documented.

Evaluated by Rego package nist.ai_rmf.main (frameworks/federal/nist/ai_rmf/nist_ai_rmf_main.rego): Intended purposes, potentially beneficial uses, context-specific laws, norms and expectations, and prospective settings in which the AI system will be deployed are understood and documented. Considerations include: the specific set or types of users along with their expectations; potential positive and negative impacts of system uses to individuals, communities, organizations, society, and the planet; assumptions and related limitations about AI system purposes, uses, and risks across the development or product AI lifecycle; and related TEVV and system metrics.

Evaluated by Rego package nist.ai_rmf.main (frameworks/federal/nist/ai_rmf/nist_ai_rmf_main.rego): Interdisciplinary AI actors, competencies, skills, and capacities for establishing context reflect demographic diversity and broad domain and user experience expertise, and their participation is documented. Opportunities for interdisciplinary collaboration are prioritized.
Evaluated by Rego package nist.ai_rmf.main (frameworks/federal/nist/ai_rmf/nist_ai_rmf_main.rego): The organization’s mission and relevant goals for AI technology are understood and documented.

Evaluated by Rego package nist.ai_rmf.main (frameworks/federal/nist/ai_rmf/nist_ai_rmf_main.rego): The business value or context of business use has been clearly defined or – in the case of assessing existing AI systems – re-evaluated.
Evaluated by Rego package nist.ai_rmf.main (frameworks/federal/nist/ai_rmf/nist_ai_rmf_main.rego): Organizational risk tolerances are determined and documented.

Evaluated by Rego package nist.ai_rmf.main (frameworks/federal/nist/ai_rmf/nist_ai_rmf_main.rego): System requirements (e.g., “the system shall respect the privacy of its users”) are elicited from and understood by relevant AI actors. Design decisions take socio-technical implications into account to address AI risks.

Evaluated by Rego package nist.ai_rmf.main (frameworks/federal/nist/ai_rmf/nist_ai_rmf_main.rego): The specific tasks and methods used to implement the tasks that the AI system will support are defined (e.g., classifiers, generative models, recommenders).

Evaluated by Rego package nist.ai_rmf.main (frameworks/federal/nist/ai_rmf/nist_ai_rmf_main.rego): Information about the AI system’s knowledge limits and how system output may be utilized and overseen by humans is documented. Documentation provides sufficient information to assist relevant AI actors when making decisions and taking subsequent actions.

Evaluated by Rego package nist.ai_rmf.main (frameworks/federal/nist/ai_rmf/nist_ai_rmf_main.rego): Scientific integrity and TEVV considerations are identified and documented, including those related to experimental design, data collection and selection (e.g., availability, representativeness, suitability), system trustworthiness, and construct validation.
Evaluated by Rego package nist.ai_rmf.main (frameworks/federal/nist/ai_rmf/nist_ai_rmf_main.rego): Potential benefits of intended AI system functionality and performance are examined and documented.

Evaluated by Rego package nist.ai_rmf.main (frameworks/federal/nist/ai_rmf/nist_ai_rmf_main.rego): Potential costs, including non-monetary costs, which result from expected or realized AI errors or system functionality and trustworthiness – as connected to organizational risk tolerance – are examined and documented.

Evaluated by Rego package nist.ai_rmf.main (frameworks/federal/nist/ai_rmf/nist_ai_rmf_main.rego): Targeted application scope is specified and documented based on the system’s capability, established context, and AI system categorization.

Evaluated by Rego package nist.ai_rmf.main (frameworks/federal/nist/ai_rmf/nist_ai_rmf_main.rego): Processes for operator and practitioner proficiency with AI system performance and trustworthiness – and relevant technical standards and certifications – are defined, assessed, and documented.

Evaluated by Rego package nist.ai_rmf.main (frameworks/federal/nist/ai_rmf/nist_ai_rmf_main.rego): Processes for human oversight are defined, assessed, and documented in accordance with organizational policies from the GOVERN function.

Evaluated by Rego package nist.ai_rmf.main (frameworks/federal/nist/ai_rmf/nist_ai_rmf_main.rego): Approaches for mapping AI technology and legal risks of its components – including the use of third-party data or software – are in place, followed, and documented, as are risks of infringement of a third party’s intellectual property or other rights.

Evaluated by Rego package nist.ai_rmf.main (frameworks/federal/nist/ai_rmf/nist_ai_rmf_main.rego): Internal risk controls for components of the AI system, including third-party AI technologies, are identified and documented.

Evaluated by Rego package nist.ai_rmf.main (frameworks/federal/nist/ai_rmf/nist_ai_rmf_main.rego): Likelihood and magnitude of each identified impact (both potentially beneficial and harmful) based on expected use, past uses of AI systems in similar contexts, public incident reports, feedback from those external to the team that developed or deployed the AI system, or other data are identified and documented.

Evaluated by Rego package nist.ai_rmf.main (frameworks/federal/nist/ai_rmf/nist_ai_rmf_main.rego): Practices and personnel for supporting regular engagement with relevant AI actors and integrating feedback about positive, negative, and unanticipated impacts are in place and documented.

implemented-requirements.description: Evaluated by Rego package pqc.cswp39 (frameworks/federal/pqc/cswp39_crypto_agility.rego): NIST CSWP 39 §§3–4, 6.1–6.3 — whether the organisation designs or implements protocols, applications, libraries, kernels, embedded or hardware cryptography must be declared true or false

Evaluated by Rego package pqc.cswp39 (frameworks/federal/pqc/cswp39_crypto_agility.rego): NIST CSWP 39 §6.4 — whether the organisation self-manages cryptography in the cloud (own HSMs or cryptographic applications in IaaS, or cloud services integrated with on-premises cryptography) must be declared true or false

Evaluated by Rego package pqc.cswp39 (frameworks/federal/pqc/cswp39_crypto_agility.rego): To achieve crypto agility, security protocol implementations should be modular so they can easily accommodate the insertion of new algorithms or cipher suites.

Evaluated by Rego package pqc.cswp39 (frameworks/federal/pqc/cswp39_crypto_agility.rego): Implementations should also provide a way to determine when deployed implementations have shifted from the old algorithms to more desirable ones.

Evaluated by Rego package pqc.cswp39 (frameworks/federal/pqc/cswp39_crypto_agility.rego): The set of mandatory-to-implement algorithms is expected to change over time, and the cipher suite negotiation mechanism needs to accommodate the identification of yet-to-be specified algorithms in the future.

Evaluated by Rego package pqc.cswp39 (frameworks/federal/pqc/cswp39_crypto_agility.rego): Designers are encouraged to pick one of these approaches and use it consistently throughout the protocol or family of protocols.

Evaluated by Rego package pqc.cswp39 (frameworks/federal/pqc/cswp39_crypto_agility.rego): To avoid these interoperability problems in the future, any aspect of the algorithm not specified by the algorithm identifiers needs to be negotiated, including the key size and other parameters.
Evaluated by Rego package pqc.cswp39 (frameworks/federal/pqc/cswp39_crypto_agility.rego): When the new algorithm is widely deployed, it should be used in lieu of the old algorithm.

Evaluated by Rego package pqc.cswp39 (frameworks/federal/pqc/cswp39_crypto_agility.rego): As part of their crypto agility efforts in the transition to PQC, security protocol designers need to plan for public keys, signatures, and key-encapsulation ciphertext to be much larger than those currently used.
Evaluated by Rego package pqc.cswp39 (frameworks/federal/pqc/cswp39_crypto_agility.rego): To be safe, security protocol designers should plan for significant growth in the size of cryptographic data.

Evaluated by Rego package pqc.cswp39 (frameworks/federal/pqc/cswp39_crypto_agility.rego): The mechanism that a security protocol uses to perform cryptographic algorithm negotiation should include integrity protection.

Evaluated by Rego package pqc.cswp39 (frameworks/federal/pqc/cswp39_crypto_agility.rego): In this case, the integrity protection should be at least as strong as that provided by a future cipher suite, which can result in the need for several mandatory-to-implement algorithms to cover the various security strength requirements.

Evaluated by Rego package pqc.cswp39 (frameworks/federal/pqc/cswp39_crypto_agility.rego): The PKI root of trust must be known to all of the relying parties to validate a certificate, and the cost of deploying a PKI root of trust is significant, so the expense associated with a transition to the use of a hybrid root of trust followed by a potential second transition to using only a PQC algorithm for a root of trust must be considered.

Evaluated by Rego package pqc.cswp39 (frameworks/federal/pqc/cswp39_crypto_agility.rego): In addition, administrators need to be aware that multiple environments are being used, track the policies, and enable the algorithms or cipher suites for each of them.

Evaluated by Rego package pqc.cswp39 (frameworks/federal/pqc/cswp39_crypto_agility.rego): Security protocol designers should perform an analysis to ensure that all security goals are achieved when each of the possible key-establishment mechanisms is used.

Evaluated by Rego package pqc.cswp39 (frameworks/federal/pqc/cswp39_crypto_agility.rego): When a protocol designer is specifying a cipher suite, the relative strength of each algorithm needs to be considered, and complexity in security protocols needs to be avoided.
Evaluated by Rego package pqc.cswp39 (frameworks/federal/pqc/cswp39_crypto_agility.rego): When selecting or negotiating a cipher suite, the relative strength of each algorithm needs to be considered.

Evaluated by Rego package pqc.cswp39 (frameworks/federal/pqc/cswp39_crypto_agility.rego): The security protections provided by each algorithm in a particular context need to be considered when making the selection.

Evaluated by Rego package pqc.cswp39 (frameworks/federal/pqc/cswp39_crypto_agility.rego): Algorithm strength needs to be considered when a security protocol is designed, implemented, deployed, and configured.
Evaluated by Rego package pqc.cswp39 (frameworks/federal/pqc/cswp39_crypto_agility.rego): Performance and security need to be balanced.

Evaluated by Rego package pqc.cswp39 (frameworks/federal/pqc/cswp39_crypto_agility.rego): Security protocol designers need to balance agility with simplicity and anticipate changes to the supported set of cryptographic algorithms over time.

Evaluated by Rego package pqc.cswp39 (frameworks/federal/pqc/cswp39_crypto_agility.rego): Security protocol implementations should be as straightforward as possible to reduce vulnerability to attacks.

Evaluated by Rego package pqc.cswp39 (frameworks/federal/pqc/cswp39_crypto_agility.rego): While support for multiple algorithms is necessary to achieve crypto agility, gratuitous options should be avoided to keep implementations from becoming unnecessary large.
Evaluated by Rego package pqc.cswp39 (frameworks/federal/pqc/cswp39_crypto_agility.rego): Furthermore, once an algorithm is disallowed, it should be removed from the protocol to reduce complexity.

Evaluated by Rego package pqc.cswp39 (frameworks/federal/pqc/cswp39_crypto_agility.rego): Implementers should periodically review the options that are actually being used and then remove unused options to keep the attack surface as small as possible.

Evaluated by Rego package pqc.cswp39 (frameworks/federal/pqc/cswp39_crypto_agility.rego): To achieve crypto agility, system designers must introduce mechanisms that simplify the replacement of cryptographic algorithms in software, libraries, hardware, firmware, and infrastructures.
